result.headline: About 80–85% of Bengaluru's dry waste passes through informal waste pickers and kabadiwalas, and the Solid Waste Management Rules 2026 (in force since 1 April 2026) now require bulk generators and sorting yards to register on a central portal and deal only with registered parties. Verifying informal players and keeping a weighed record of every hand-off is the one capability almost every persona needs.

findings.point: Most recyclables pass through informal hands, so informal micro-businesses are the core users.
findings.detail: India's informal recycling sector is about 4 million people. That includes an estimated 2.2 million waste pickers, 76.2% of them informally employed, who collect 15–20% of city waste (GRID-Arendal/IAWP 2024). A study hosted by BBMP (the former Bengaluru city corporation) put the informal share of Bengaluru's dry waste at 80–85%. Daily volumes by tier: 80–100 kg per waste picker, 250–300 kg for an average scrap dealer, 1–5 t for a medium aggregator, 10–20 t for a large one and 25–30 t for a very large one. Each of the 4–5 hand-offs is a separate small business, which matches the roles Luma.Green onboards.

findings.point: The SWM Rules 2026 make 'registered and on the portal' a condition of trading for bulk generators, sorting yards and cities.
findings.detail: Notified 27 Jan 2026 (S.O. 388(E)); in force since 1 Apr 2026. Households must separate waste into four streams (wet, dry, sanitary, special care) and hand it to authorised waste pickers or collectors. Gated communities and institutions over 5,000 m², all RWAs, hotels and restaurants have one year (to Jan 2027) to send recyclables only to authorised pickers or recyclers. A bulk waste generator is anyone with ≥20,000 m² floor area, ≥40,000 L of water a day or ≥100 kg of waste a day. It must register on the central portal, meet Extended Bulk Waste Generator Responsibility (EBWGR), file returns by 30 June and must not engage unregistered entities (r.6). Any entity sorting dry waste must register with the local body, report quarterly by the 15th and not deal with unregistered parties (r.9). Cities must keep a ward-wise database of waste pickers and informal collectors on the portal and set up a way to recognise them (r.39(53)–(54)). The rules' 'informal waste collector' explicitly includes waste traders who buy and sell recyclables, which covers kabadiwalas.

findings.point: Households are online and prefer Indian languages, but many share phones and fewer than half pay digitally.
findings.detail: IAMAI-Kantar ICUBE 2024 counts 886 million active internet users: 488 m rural, 397 m urban, 47% women. 98% used content in Indian languages, and 57% of urban users prefer them to English. 20% go online on someone else's phone (15% urban, 24% rural), and 59% of these shared-phone users are women. 140 million use voice commands. Only 405 million (about 46%) made digital payments. So the household flow should keep one SMS code per booking (no account), a tracking link that opens on any phone, read-aloud, and cash as a full payment option.

findings.point: Bengaluru speaks more than 'Kannada, Hindi, English'.
findings.detail: Census 2011 mother tongues for the city: Kannada 42.1% (3.57 m), Tamil 1.39 m, Telugu 1.17 m, Urdu 1.10 m, Hindi 0.48 m, Malayalam 0.27 m, Marathi 0.17 m. Tamil, Telugu and Urdu speakers each outnumber Hindi speakers more than two to one. In the waste trade, the BBMP-hosted study counted 50,000–60,000 Bengali-speaking migrant waste pickers (Marathahalli, Bellandur, Sarjapur Road, Bommanahalli) and a large community of Marwari traders. All these languages are already among Luma.Green's 12; the pilot should check them first.

findings.point: Kabadiwalas run on relationships, advances and cash, and customers distrust their scales.
findings.detail: Scrap dealers pay waste pickers advances to lock in supply and have standing arrangements with a larger aggregator. Margins are around ₹2/kg on cartons, with 'no real accounting'. Large aggregators depend on immediate cash. Traders pay sellers at once but wait for processors to pay them. Many dealers in Jolly Mohalla (Bengaluru's scrap market) had no BBMP licence and were wary of outsiders. Weighing is disputed: in the 17 months to Aug 2024, Karnataka's weights-and-measures department (Legal Metrology) made 20,391 inspections in Bengaluru Urban, booked 5,375 cases and fined ₹1.79 crore. Scales whose official stamp was not renewed were a common violation. An itemised, weighed receipt builds trust on both sides.

findings.point: GST rules on metal scrap change who files tax paperwork at the kabadiwala → yard hand-off.
findings.detail: The 54th GST Council (9 Sep 2024) made two changes. When an unregistered seller sells metal scrap to a registered buyer, the buyer now pays the GST (reverse charge), even if the seller is below the registration threshold. And B2B metal-scrap sales between registered businesses now carry 2% TDS (tax deducted by the buyer). GSTN's 22 Oct 2024 advisory tells metal-scrap buyers to register as tax deductors (GST REG-07, 'Metal Scrap Dealers', Notification 25/2024). So yards buying from mostly unregistered kabadiwalas carry this paperwork. Records need each seller's GST status (onboarding already captures 'not GST-registered') and the material type.

findings.point: Bengaluru's waste pickers are organised but short of documents; the city's ward-level Dry Waste Collection Centres (DWCCs) could serve as ready-made yards and Saathi pools.
findings.detail: BBMP opened 198 ward DWCCs in 2012–13. By Sep 2025, 141 remained and 119 were running, serving 127 wards; Hasiru Dala (a Bengaluru waste-picker NGO) supports 35. Waste-picker ID cards issued in 2013 were valid for ten years and have expired, and the 2020 DWCC agreements (MoUs) with BBMP have lapsed. Many migrant pickers lack documents and some cannot get Aadhaar. A DWCC usually has 20–25 pickers and can earn up to ₹1.5 lakh in a good month, split by hours worked, but only about 30% of incoming waste is good enough to earn from. Operators borrow informally or pledge gold to cover vehicle costs. A registered Karnataka waste-pickers' union has 2,300+ members. In Sep 2025 the Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA) replaced BBMP and waste moved to Bengaluru Solid Waste Management Ltd (BSWML), leaving the DWCCs' future unclear. Pickers are wary of new apps (ecoSansar, NoKasa) that don't treat them as partners.

findings.point: Dispatching or paying Saathis through an app is now regulated 'aggregator' work, in Karnataka and nationally.
findings.detail: Karnataka's Platform-Based Gig Workers Act 2025 covers app-booked work, including home services and e-commerce. Platforms must register, pay a welfare fee (the state set 1% of the worker's payout, capped per transaction), and communicate in Kannada, English or a language the worker understands. In July 2026 the High Court refused to stay the act and ordered Swiggy, Zomato, Blinkit and Zepto to deposit their fees for the second quarter. Nationally, the Social Security (Central) Rules 2026 (in force 8 May 2026) require aggregators to register, report every new worker and every exit in real time, and contribute either a notified share of turnover or 5% of payouts. Workers qualify for benefits after 90 days with one aggregator, or 120 days across several. Keeping Saathi pay off-platform, as planned, limits exposure for now; the job-matching model needs a legal read before a Saathi pilot.

findings.point: UPI stays free for households, but from 15 Oct 2026 business payments above ₹2,000 cost the receiving business 0.4%, unless it is a small merchant.
findings.detail: NPCI's new fee (MDR) is 0.4% on UPI payments to a business above ₹2,000, capped at ₹300 for payments of ₹75,000 or more. Free: person-to-person transfers, AutoPay, and small merchants (P2PM) receiving up to ₹1 lakh a month through UPI. Apps may not charge customers. Along the chain: kabadiwala → household payouts are person-to-person and free; yard → kabadiwala payments are free while the kabadiwala stays a small merchant; recycler → yard and bulk-generator vendor payments will often pay the fee. The fee starts during the pilot week (13–20 Oct), so recording the method (cash / UPI person-to-person / UPI merchant) will show whether it shifts trades back to cash.

findings.point: Bulk generators, RWAs and city officials pay for compliance and reporting, not for scrap prices.
findings.detail: Hasiru Dala Innovations (the NGO's commercial arm) sells to Bengaluru bulk generators on alignment with the SWM rules, 'pay for what you generate' pricing, GPS-tracked collection with 99% regularity, structured impact reports and brand partnerships (Unilever, H&M). A client housing society points to its BSWML empanelment. The national cleanliness ranking, Swachh Survekshan 2025-26, has 12,500 marks: 1,000 for segregation, collection and transport, and 150 for waste processing at bulk generators, scored partly on whether all third-party vendors are empanelled. With SWM returns due 30 June, these buyers need verified vendors and exportable records of kilograms by waste stream.

findings.point: Brands with plastic-packaging obligations (EPR) and their auditors face a trust crisis that verified chain-of-custody data could help fix.
findings.detail: Under the central pollution board's (CPCB) EPR guidelines, producers, importers, brand owners (together, PIBOs) and plastic waste processors must register on the central portal and may not trade with unregistered entities (6.2–6.3). CPCB or state boards, directly or through a designated agency, verify them by inspection and periodic audit; processors file returns by 30 April. Rigid (Category I) packaging must contain 30% recycled plastic in 2025-26, rising to 40%, 50% and 60% by 2028-29. The Centre for Science and Environment (CSE) found 41,577 PIBO registrations and 700,000 fake certificates issued by plastic recyclers, 38 times their capacity. Fines totalled ₹355 crore, and informal collectors have no place in EPR. Brands and auditors value evidence from the source (photos, weights, GPS, counterparties), but Luma.Green should not issue certificates itself.

findings.point: Manufacturers want domestic feedstock that is graded, traceable and tax-compliant.
findings.detail: India used about 41 Mt of iron and steel scrap in FY2024-25 and imported roughly a quarter of it. Scrap feeds 23% of steel output against a 50% target for 2047, and by March 2025, 48 countries had restricted scrap exports. The Material Recycling Association of India (MRAI) says: the informal sector undercuts formal recyclers by avoiding 18% GST; India lacks uniform grading and certification; and nothing traces scrap from origin to end use. Steelmakers that ran their own collection could keep margins of up to 16% that now go to intermediaries (EY-Parthenon). The roadmap's recycler → manufacturer 'order ahead' view fits this persona.

findings.point: Investors, lenders and CSR teams each need a different proof from the same record of trades.
findings.detail: Investors compare against players like Recykal: FY26 gross revenue ₹1,498 crore (+53% year on year), operating losses cut from 6% to 4%, and a USD 23 m bridge round in June 2026 (Circulate Capital exited at 5x). Lenders face a cash trade: DWCC operators pledge gold or borrow informally, and traders pay sellers upfront but are paid late by processors. Verified trade histories could later support lending to cover that gap. CSR applies to companies with ≥₹500 crore net worth, ≥₹1,000 crore turnover or ≥₹5 crore net profit. They must spend 2% of average net profit, environmental sustainability is an eligible area (Schedule VII), and they need verified outcomes such as kilograms diverted and livelihoods supported.

findings.point: The Luma.Green team's own roles are shaped by the data-protection rules and a growing verification checklist.
findings.detail: The Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Rules were notified on 14 Nov 2025 with 18 months to comply (to about May 2027). They require: a separate plain-language consent notice; breach notices to the people affected; a published contact for data questions; and answers to access, correction and erasure requests within 90 days. Penalties reach ₹250 crore for weak security. Consequences by role: support needs a data-rights queue in 12 languages; verification must add SWM-portal/local-body registration, CPCB EPR or processor numbers and metal-scrap TDS status to today's GST and pollution-board checks; finance must track payment method and the UPI fee; compliance must track gig-law status. One admin does all of this in the pilot.

recommendations.feature: Demo world: one login per persona, plus read-only observer logins
recommendations.why: Investors judge breadth by clicking through each persona, and the founder asked for test IDs. Put Bengaluru demo data in one editable seed file so numbers are easy to change: wards, 6 kabadiwalas, 2 yards, 1 DWCC, 1 recycler, 1 manufacturer, 3 Saathis, 1 bulk generator and 1 RWA. Read-only observer logins (city, brand/auditor, CSR, lender, investor) show the non-trading personas without building new flows.

recommendations.feature: Material passport: trace one bale back to the household pickups it came from
recommendations.why: Brands and auditors are reeling from 700,000 fake EPR certificates, and MRAI names missing traceability as a core gap. One screen showing kilograms, price, date, place and verified badges at each hand-off (household → kabadiwala → yard → recycler → manufacturer) demonstrates the 'record every hand-off' principle.

recommendations.feature: Pilot numbers page for investors
recommendations.why: Build it from the existing events table (ADR 0012): kilograms and rupees through the platform, completed pickups, time to accept, estimated vs weighed kilograms, verified organisations by role, repeat households. Investors compare against players at Recykal's scale and want traction, not a feature list.

recommendations.feature: Registrations stored as editable data on every organisation, plus an optional 'registered sellers only' switch per buyer
recommendations.why: SWM 2026 (r.6(g), r.9(5)) and the EPR guidelines (6.3) bar registered entities from dealing with unregistered ones. Store each organisation's registrations as rows: GSTIN, pollution-board consent with expiry, CPCB EPR/processor number, SWM-portal or local-body registration, recognised-collector status, metal-scrap tax-deductor registration, Udyam (MSME) number. Buyers who must comply can switch on the filter without the platform shutting out unregistered kabadiwalas.

recommendations.feature: Bengaluru language pack and read-aloud
recommendations.why: Tamil, Telugu and Urdu speakers each outnumber Hindi speakers more than two to one in Bengaluru, and 50–60k waste pickers speak Bengali. Hand-check Kannada, English, Tamil, Telugu, Urdu, Hindi and Bengali first, order the language grid to match, and add read-aloud to every kabadiwala and Saathi action (140 m Indian internet users already use voice).

recommendations.feature: Weigh-and-pay trust kit
recommendations.why: Scale disputes are common: 5,375 weights-and-measures cases in Bengaluru Urban in 17 months. Record the scale's official stamp expiry at onboarding, allow a photo of the scale display per weighing, send an itemised SMS receipt (kg × rate), and add a one-tap dispute that reaches support.

recommendations.feature: Payment method and UPI-fee type on every recorded payment
recommendations.why: From 15 Oct 2026, UPI business payments above ₹2,000 cost 0.4% unless the receiver is a small merchant, and fewer than half of internet users pay digitally. Record cash / UPI person-to-person / UPI merchant, keep money off-platform, and watch whether business-to-business hand-offs slide back to cash.

recommendations.feature: Saathi onboarding built for real waste pickers, with an NGO partner
recommendations.why: Old BBMP picker IDs have expired and many migrants lack Aadhaar. Accept a voter ID, an expired picker card, or a letter from an NGO, DWCC or union, plus a selfie. Pilot with a Hasiru Dala-supported DWCC as the first yard and Saathi pool. Keep Saathi pay off-platform until lawyers confirm whether Luma.Green counts as an 'aggregator' under Karnataka's gig act and the national Social Security Code.

recommendations.feature: Compliance module for bulk generators and RWAs
recommendations.why: SWM 2026 makes large offices, hotels, malls, hospitals and campuses register, use registered vendors and file returns by 30 June; RWAs have until Jan 2027. What these buyers pay for (as Hasiru Dala Innovations shows) is scheduled pickups by verified vendors, monthly kilograms by stream and proof of vendor registration.

recommendations.feature: Exports of the waste-picker and kabadiwala registry for cities and NGOs
recommendations.why: Local bodies must keep a ward-wise database of waste pickers and informal collectors on the central portal, updated by 30 June each year. With consent, Luma.Green's verified kabadiwala and Saathi records and DWCC volumes can feed it, which makes the city a partner.

recommendations.feature: Evidence packs for brands and auditors, sold through registered processors
recommendations.why: A read-only audit login with the audit log, photos, GPS, timestamps, weights and each counterparty's registrations, offered to brands through registered plastic processors. Luma.Green should never issue EPR certificates itself, given the fraud history.

recommendations.feature: Consent-based sharing of trade history with lenders
recommendations.why: DWCCs and traders fund working capital informally (gold pledges, processors paying late). A consented export of verified trade history can later let banks and NBFCs lend to kabadiwalas and yards.

risks: Luma.Green could count as an 'aggregator' under Karnataka's gig act or the national Social Security Code if it dispatches or pays Saathis. That brings registration, a 1% welfare fee, real-time worker reporting, contributions up to 5% of payouts, and a duty to communicate in Kannada.

'Registered-only' rules (SWM 2026 r.6(g) and r.9(5); EPR 6.3) could shut unregistered kabadiwalas out of bulk-generator and brand-linked trade. Ignoring the rules makes the platform unusable for business buyers; enforcing them too early loses the informal supply.
IDs, selfies and home locations of migrant waste pickers, who fear eviction and harassment, could harm them if leaked. Weak security can draw data-protection penalties up to ₹250 crore.
Recorded weights and prices can be gamed (inflated kilograms, fake pickups). If platform records ever feed credits, the 700,000 fake EPR certificates show how this can go wrong.
The UPI fee from 15 Oct 2026 (during the pilot week) and GST reverse charge/TDS on metal scrap may push business hand-offs back to cash and off the platform, thinning the data trail.

Bengaluru's institutions are in flux: BBMP gave way to the Greater Bengaluru Authority and five corporations, waste moved to BSWML, and DWCC agreements lapsed. City and DWCC partnerships are uncertain during the pilot.
The 12-language promise may miss the languages the Bengaluru pilot actually needs (Tamil, Telugu, Urdu, Bengali) if those are checked last; users with low literacy need voice, not just translation.
A single admin verifying every role within 12–24 hours will not scale once bulk generators, brands and auditors join.
openQuestions: Does a scrap-pickup marketplace or Saathi job board fall under Karnataka's gig act ('home services' or 'e-marketplace') or the Social Security Code's definition of an aggregator?
Which SWM 2026 registration should pilot yards (and Luma.Green) hold with GBA/BSWML, and will GBA recognise kabadiwalas as 'authorised' informal waste collectors?
Will a Hasiru Dala-supported DWCC or the Karnataka waste-pickers' union co-run the pilot as a yard and Saathi pool?
How many pilot kabadiwalas accept UPI, and do they stay under the ₹1 lakh a month small-merchant limit that avoids the new UPI fee?
What evidence from informal collection would a brand's EPR auditor accept (photo, weight, GPS, counterparty registration), and would brands pay for it?
Do Bengaluru RWAs and tech parks expect to be paid for dry waste or to pay for compliant collection, and what report format does BSWML ask of them?
Which ID or attestation can undocumented migrant waste pickers provide, and will an NGO's attestation be enough for verification?
What are recycle points worth, and could CSR budgets fund them?

result.headline: One yard-to-factory truckload already needs about six documents (purchase order, weighbridge slip, quality report, receipt note, GST invoice, e-way bill), kept across Tally, WhatsApp and paper. A CPCB audit also found a Karnataka recycler that issued recycling certificates for 3.48 lakh tonnes while its plant was not running. So Luma.Green should record each hand-off once, as evidence, and export it in Tally and CPCB formats, not try to replace factory software.

findings.point: Tally is the back office, and its purchase flow already matches a scrap hand-off
findings.detail: Tally says 2.7 million+ businesses use it, and it advertises built-in e-invoice, e-way bill and WhatsApp sharing. Its purchase cycle runs: Purchase Order, Receipt Note (goods received), Rejection Out, Purchase voucher, Debit Note. Tracking numbers link each receipt to its bill. A 'Purchase Bills Pending' report catches goods received but not billed, and the reverse. TallyPrime imports Excel (.xlsx/.xls, using mapping templates, with ready templates for Busy, Marg, QuickBooks, Odoo, Shopify, Sage and Amazon data), XML and JSON. Before committing it lists exceptions such as missing fields, wrong GST details and duplicates. So each Luma.Green trade can map one-to-one to Tally vouchers and be handed over as a file.

findings.point: Tally runs on the customer's own PC, so exporting files is the easy integration and live sync is harder
findings.detail: TallyPrime answers XML requests only while it is running. It acts as an HTTP server on the local machine (default port 9000, switched on in its settings), and each request is an ENVELOPE/HEADER/BODY message with TALLYREQUEST set to Import or Export. A cloud app on Vercel and Convex cannot reach that port without a small local agent or add-on. Tally's own help also describes XML/JSON import mainly as a way to move data between Tally installations. For the pilot: download a file, then import it in Tally. A connector is a scale-stage feature.

findings.point: WhatsApp is how the trade already works; the paid API charges per message, and web sharing is free
findings.detail: Tally sells 'TallyPrime with WhatsApp Business' for sending invoices. Since 1 July 2025 Meta charges for each template message delivered. Service replies are free. Utility templates are free inside an open customer-service window (24 hours after the user's last message). India moved to INR billing on 1 Jan 2026, and every Indian WhatsApp Business account must switch to INR by 31 Dec 2026 or Meta stops delivering its messages. The browser's Web Share API lets an installed web app pass a PDF or CSV straight to WhatsApp on Chrome for Android and Safari on iOS. It is free and needs no template approval, but desktop support is limited.

findings.point: Moving a load: the e-way bill rule puts the paperwork on the yard when it buys from an unregistered kabadiwala
findings.detail: Under CGST Rule 138, a registered person moving goods worth more than ₹50,000 must create an e-way bill before the truck leaves. Part B, the vehicle details, is needed for road movement. When an unregistered supplier sells to a registered buyer, the buyer counts as causing the movement if the buyer is known when the goods start moving. Most kabadiwalas are unregistered (GST is optional in Luma.Green's own onboarding), so the yard usually has to raise the e-way bill. A bill is valid one day per 200 km. The dispatch step should therefore record the e-way bill number and vehicle number together with the weighbridge slip.

findings.point: Metal scrap has carried extra tax steps since October 2024, and each creates a task per trade
findings.detail: Four rules now apply to metal scrap. (1) From 10 Oct 2024, a registered buyer pays GST under reverse charge on metal scrap (Customs Tariff chapters 72 to 81) bought from an unregistered seller (Notification 06/2024-CT(Rate)). (2) The buyer must issue a self-invoice within 30 days of receiving the goods (Rule 47A, in force from 1 Nov 2024). (3) From 10 Oct 2024, a registered buyer of metal scrap from a registered seller must deduct GST TDS (Notification 25/2024-CT). Section 51 sets this at 1% CGST, plus the matching 1% state tax, on contracts above ₹2.5 lakh. (4) The Finance Bill 2026 memorandum proposed raising income-tax TCS on sale of scrap from 1% to 2% from 1 Apr 2026, under Section 394(1) of the new Income-tax Act. Accounts teams at yards and recyclers track all of this by hand today. A platform can flag these steps and pre-fill monthly registers, but it should not file anything.

findings.point: CPCB's EPR portal fixes the data a recycler's compliance person must key in
findings.detail: Every plastic-waste purchase needs: supplier name and address, EPR category (I to IV), quantity in kg or tonnes, date, and the supplier's GSTIN (or PAN/Aadhaar if unregistered), plus a copy of the invoice. Production entries use a conversion factor confirmed at physical verification. Certificates come in lots of 1, 10, 50, 100, 500 or 1,000 tonnes. A sale of recycled output counts only with a signed GST e-invoice (buyer and seller GSTIN, IRN, HSN, amount, QR code), which CPCB checks against GSTN. Processors file annual returns by 30 April. They cannot certify more than their installed capacity, and false data means a one-year debarment. Demand comes from brand owners, who must use recycled plastic in rigid (Category I) packaging: 30% in 2025-26, 40% in 2026-27, 50% in 2027-28 and 60% from 2028-29. Category II rises from 10% to 20% and Category III from 5% to 10%.

findings.point: Karnataka is where weak chain-of-custody records turned into a scandal
findings.detail: A CPCB audit (reported 8 Nov 2023) found that Enviro Recyclean in Ramanagara, cleared by KSPCB to process 3.5 lakh tonnes a year, had transferred EPR certificates for 3.48 lakh tonnes while the plant was not yet running. The audit called the invoices it had uploaded 'fallacious'. The proposed penalty was ₹5,000 a tonne, more than ₹174 crore. The audit also noted the plant had received its consent to operate within seven working days of its consent to establish. KSPCB then put all 89 recyclers it had cleared under inspection, and about 140 units had applied. Buyers and brand owners will value evidence tied to each load: weighbridge slips, vehicle numbers, photos, and checks that output never exceeds input.

findings.point: Weight and quality disputes follow written trade rules, and Bengaluru's scales are actively policed
findings.detail: The ISRI scrap specifications (now published by ReMA) say, for paper, that the buyer's weight governs if taken on a certified scale. There is no adjustment when the gap is 1% or less for domestic loads (2% for export). Above that, the seller can ask for a review by producing a certified gross/tare/net ticket or a bale-by-bale tally. Paper should be at most 12% moisture unless buyer and seller agree otherwise before shipping, including how to test it. For old corrugated containers (OCC), prohibitive materials must not exceed 1%, and outthrows plus prohibitives must not exceed 5%. In Bengaluru Urban, Legal Metrology made 20,391 inspections in the 17 months to August 2024. It booked 5,375 cases and collected ₹1.79 crore in fines, and unrenewed stamping was among the most common violations. Luma.Green should record both parties' weights, the slip photo and the scale's stamping date, and should treat quality deductions as data.

findings.point: Recycled-content certificates certify each site along the chain; Luma.Green can supply the evidence but cannot issue them
findings.detail: GRS and RCS rely on third-party audits at each stage of the chain. GRS covers business-to-business claims from 20% recycled content, but a consumer-facing label needs 50%. Textile Exchange is merging them into its Materials Matter Standard, effective 31 Dec 2026 and mandatory from 31 Dec 2027. ISCC PLUS offers three tracking methods: mass balance, physical segregation and controlled blending. Each site holds its own certificate, valid for 12 months. Collecting points, processing units and traders that store material must be certified; transporters need not be. What helps a certified recycler pass its audit is lot-level data: lot IDs, input and output weights, supplier site and dates, which Luma.Green can hold. Luma.Green should not present its records as certificates.

findings.point: Karnataka's pollution-board consents can be checked in a public register
findings.detail: KSPCB's XGN consent register is public. For each unit it lists PCB ID, name, colour category (Red, Orange, Green or White), regional office, consent type (consent to establish, consent to operate, hazardous-waste authorisation, combined order), status (granted or rejected), consent number and validity date. The newest entries were dated 28 Sep 2026. The admin can check the number and validity on an uploaded consent PDF against this register. Luma.Green can then store the validity date and remind the compliance person before it expires.

findings.point: Competitors already offer a document pack for every trade
findings.detail: Recykal Market advertises sellers checked against GST records, the invoice, e-way bill and weight certificate in one dashboard, an automated audit pack, a grade guarantee and payment protection. Attero's MetalMandi launched in 2025. By April 2026 it had 1.1 lakh registered users, 50,000+ monthly active users and about 15,000 tonnes a month of metal scrap, with live prices, AI grading from photos, document uploads, geo-tracking and shipment monitoring. Its main hubs are Delhi NCR, Chennai, Mumbai, Pune and Hyderabad; Bengaluru is not among them. A document pack is now expected by default. Luma.Green's advantage has to be origin back to the household and kabadiwala, a Kannada-first interface and trustworthy weighing in Bengaluru.

findings.point: Many of Bengaluru's own recyclers are informal and unregistered
findings.detail: In June 2025 the Deccan Herald reported that recyclers in Nayandahalli, Kumbalagodu and Bidadi are small, unorganised and unregistered. Only 20-30% of the city's plastic is recycled, and only about 40% of the plastic reaching dry-waste collection centres. A recycler who puts in ₹10 lakh to start cannot afford a ₹50 lakh effluent treatment plant. Luma.Green's rule that recyclers upload a pollution-board consent will screen many of these out. The first factory users are therefore likely to be the registered minority, and records must be captured on a phone at the moment of weighing, not in ERP-style forms.

findings.point: For finance teams, late payment is the main pain, and the law sets a 45-day limit
findings.detail: The MSMED Act requires buyers to pay micro and small suppliers within the agreed period, which cannot exceed 45 days. Late payment carries compound interest, with monthly rests, at three times the RBI bank rate. The government's MSME Samadhaan portal shows 2,56,892 delayed-payment cases filed, with ₹31,690 crore payable. Yards (as sellers) care about due dates, and buyers care about staying compliant. Storing the Udyam number and showing a due date and an overdue badge is cheap and valued by both sides.

recommendations.feature: Trade document pack: one timeline per trade (PO number, weigh-in and weigh-out slip photos, quality result, receipt/GRN number, invoice number and IRN, e-way bill number, payment reference) with a one-tap PDF in English plus the user's language. In the prototype, simulated escrow releases on the buyer's receipt (net weight after deductions).
recommendations.why: This is how factories already run a purchase (Tally: PO, then Receipt Note, then Purchase voucher), and competitors advertise the same 'invoice, e-way bill and weight certificate in one place'. It needs only optional fields on the existing trades table.

recommendations.feature: Lot traceability with a mass-balance check: lot IDs from kabadiwala sorting runs to yard bales to recycler input, a trace view back to household pickups, and a warning when a business sells more than it received or more than its declared capacity.
recommendations.why: The Karnataka case (certificates for 3.48 lakh tonnes from a plant that was not running) and CPCB's installed-capacity cap make this the credibility story for investors. ISCC PLUS and GRS audits also need lot-level evidence.

recommendations.feature: Factory team roles: the owner invites staff by phone number, and each gets a preset role (owner, purchase, gate/weighbridge, quality, accounts, compliance, plant) that opens on its own screen.
recommendations.why: A factory's work is spread across several people, but memberships currently only has owner and staff. A small enum change lets the demo show every role inside a factory.

recommendations.feature: Export centre. Now: CSV and Excel downloads laid out like Tally's sample import files for Purchase, Receipt Note and Sales vouchers (material code, English name, HSN, kg, rate, amount, party GSTIN), plus a monthly 'EPR procurement register' CSV in CPCB portal field order. Pilot: add Tally XML after testing with 2-3 real accountants.
recommendations.why: Tally already imports Excel, XML and JSON and reports errors before committing, and the CPCB fields are fixed. Exports need no API and can be built client-side or through a Convex HTTP action.

recommendations.feature: Share to WhatsApp and email: the Web Share API passes the slip or pack PDF and CSVs to WhatsApp on phones; on desktop, download plus a mailto link. wa.me text links for status updates.
recommendations.why: Free, no template approval, and it works in the installable web app today. WhatsApp is where yards and buyers already talk.

recommendations.feature: Gate and weighbridge screen (phone, Kannada first): weigh-in and weigh-out against an order, with vehicle number, gross/tare/net, slip photo and the scale's stamping-valid-until date. It compares the seller's and buyer's net weights and flags gaps over 1%.
recommendations.why: The ISRI paper rules settle disputes on certified-scale weights with a 1% domestic tolerance, and Bengaluru Legal Metrology finds many unstamped or tampered scales. Recording both weights plus the photo is the cheapest fraud control.

recommendations.feature: Quality check with deductions: parameters and default limits per material (paper moisture 12%; OCC prohibitives 1% and outthrows plus prohibitives 5%; plastics moisture, contamination and colour), with accept, deduct or reject. Deductions change the receipt weight or price, and the seller sees the reason and photos at once.
recommendations.why: Quality deductions are where money and trust are lost between yard and mill. Recording them as data also gives the investor story on grade quality.

recommendations.feature: Add fields to the material catalogue (data only, no code change): HSN code, GST unit code (e.g. KGS), EPR plastic category I to IV, a reference grade (ISRI/ReMA name), and per-organisation alias names ('raddi', buyer grade names).
recommendations.why: Invoices and Tally imports need HSN codes and units, the CPCB register needs the category, and buyers use their own grade names. The catalogue is already seeded from convex/lib/catalogue.ts, so this stays easy to change.

recommendations.feature: Tax and paperwork flags on each trade, with no filing: e-way bill needed (over ₹50,000; the buyer raises it when the seller is unregistered); metal-scrap reverse charge, self-invoice due within 30 days; GST TDS on metal scrap between registered parties above ₹2.5 lakh; TCS on scrap at the current rate. Rates and thresholds sit in an admin-editable table with effective dates, like price floors.
recommendations.why: The rules changed in Oct-Nov 2024 and again from Apr 2026 (TCS 1% to 2%, as proposed). Keeping them as dated data follows the founders' 'easy to change' rule and avoids tax-filing liability.

recommendations.feature: Compliance vault and reminders: consent number, colour category and validity (checked by the admin against the public KSPCB XGN register), EPR/PWP registration, installed capacity, the 30 April annual-return date, and document expiry alerts. One click builds an audit pack (all documents for a period, zipped).
recommendations.why: Compliance staff juggle the XGN and CPCB portals and folders of PDFs. The consent-validity data is public in Karnataka, which makes verification cheap.

recommendations.feature: Payables and receivables with the MSME 45-day clock: Udyam number on the organisation, due date set to the earlier of the agreed date and 45 days, overdue badges, and the payment reference recorded (money stays off-platform, per ADR 0009).
recommendations.why: Late payment is the MSME sector's largest dispute category (2.57 lakh cases, ₹31,690 crore). It matters to both yards and manufacturers and needs no payment licence.

recommendations.feature: Deeper integrations: a Tally connector (TDL add-on or local agent using Tally's XML/JSON HTTP interface), CSV over SFTP or an API for SAP/ERP plants, e-invoice and e-way bill generation through a GST Suvidha Provider (GSP), WhatsApp Business API utility templates billed in INR through a Meta partner, data exports for GRS and ISCC PLUS auditors, and a CPCB EPR portal feed if an API appears.
recommendations.why: Each needs credentials, local installs or vendor contracts. They pay off only once factories trade on the platform regularly.

risks: Tax rules change often: metal-scrap reverse charge and TDS arrived in Oct 2024, and TCS on scrap was proposed to double from 1 Apr 2026. Hard-coded logic or advice-like wording creates liability, so show flags with 'confirm with your CA' and keep rates as dated data.

A platform record can be faked just as EPR invoices were. Without photo evidence, both parties confirming the weight, and mass-balance alerts, Luma.Green could end up laundering bad data instead of proving good data.

Presenting Luma.Green's records as 'certificates' or trading EPR credits would clash with CPCB's authorisation of EPR trading platforms and with the GRS/ISCC certification bodies. Stay a data layer that certified parties draw on.

A live Tally sync means installing and supporting a local agent on customers' PCs, a security and support burden for a small team, and Tally versions vary across customers. Exporting files avoids this.
WhatsApp Business API adds per-message costs and template approvals, and Indian accounts must move to INR billing by 31 Dec 2026. WhatsApp groups themselves cannot be automated.

CPCB asks for PAN or Aadhaar of unregistered suppliers. Storing kabadiwalas' Aadhaar numbers raises data-protection (DPDP) risk: collect only when a recycler needs it for EPR, mask it, and limit access to the compliance role.
Requiring pollution-board consent screens out many of Bengaluru's small, unregistered recyclers, so early factory adoption may be thin. Start with registered yards and recyclers.
Recykal Market and MetalMandi already offer document dashboards at scale. Without upstream origin data and Kannada-first weighing, Luma.Green looks like a late copy.

Exports in Indian scripts can break matching against Tally masters, and Tally's document-reading AI (Docs by Ira) reads only English, non-handwritten documents. Always include material codes and English names in exports and PDFs.
openQuestions: Which accounting software do the pilot yards and recyclers use (Tally, Busy, Marg, Excel), and which Tally release? This decides between Excel and XML exports.
Do pilot yards weigh on their own stamped weighbridge, a public weighbridge or platform scales, and does their slip carry a serial number?
What grade names, quality parameters and deduction rules do Bengaluru buyers write on POs today (ISRI names, mill specs, local names)?
For metal, do pilot yards buy from unregistered kabadiwalas, and do they issue reverse-charge self-invoices today?
Do pilot recyclers hold CPCB processor (PWP) registration, and does the portal accept bulk uploads from processors, or only the per-invoice 'Single Entry' form the manual shows?
Will buyers, GRS/ISCC auditors or CPCB physical verification accept Luma.Green's weight and photo record as supporting evidence?
What TCS rate on scrap did the Finance Act 2026 actually enact, what is Karnataka's intra-state e-way bill limit, and is the 45-day MSME payment rule kept under the Income-tax Act 2025?
Which factory roles will actually log in during the pilot: only the owner, or also gate, quality and accounts staff?
Should brand owners and auditors get read-only trace links in the investor demo, and who controls sharing them?

result.headline: Household pickups can't pay for hired transport: Porter's cheapest Bengaluru mini-truck starts at ₹230 a trip, over ₹9/kg for a 25 kg household lot when newspaper fetches ₹10/kg. So Luma.Green should batch household pickups on kabadiwalas' own vehicles and put its logistics features into pooled kabadiwala-to-yard loads, with verified weights and e-way bill checks.

findings.point: Household pickups are slow and small, so they can't pay for a hired vehicle.
findings.detail: Recykal's household app Uzed reached 500,000 downloads and about 1,000 orders a day in Hyderabad and Pune. Each pickup took 45–60 minutes to count and weigh, and every trip lost money. In 2019 Recykal moved to bulk generators and left the transport to partner kabadiwalas (Forbes India, 2 Sep 2021). The Kabadiwala charges for pickups under 15 kg. Its Bengaluru partner app, Scrapr, already asks the household to choose a vehicle that fits the load before choosing a partner. Porter's Bengaluru starting fares, before distance charges: ₹150 for an e-loader (350 kg), ₹205 for a three-wheeler (500 kg), ₹230 for a Tata Ace (750 kg) and ₹330 for an 8-ft pickup. So a 25 kg household lot in a hired Tata Ace costs at least ₹9.2/kg, while The Kabadiwala pays ₹10/kg for newspaper and ₹3/kg for cartons in Bengaluru. Household pickups have to go on the kabadiwala's own handcart, cycle or auto, several pickups per trip.

findings.point: In Bengaluru both hand-off patterns exist: small dealers deliver in their own vehicles, and bigger aggregators send their own collectors.
findings.detail:
A Nov 2014 study for BBMP (by Social Venture Partners) found:
- Medium scrap dealers handle 250–300 kg a day, and most own small vehicles.
- Medium aggregators (1–5 t/day) ship weekly because they lack storage, e.g. from Munnekolala to Jolly Mohalla or Whitefield.
- One large aggregator on Harlur Road (10–20 t/day tier) employed 4 people just to collect from smaller aggregators under fixed tie-ups.
- Very large aggregators (25–30 t/day) bale before selling.
- A carton trader moving 5–10 t/day to Jigani earned about ₹2/kg, including transport and labour.
- Dealers refused low-density plastics and thermocol because they take too much space for their weight.

So the kabadiwala-to-yard flow needs both 'I'll deliver' and 'yard collects', and load planning must count volume as well as kilograms. The data is from 2014; re-check volumes in the pilot.

findings.point: Road freight costs about ₹3.7 per tonne-km, and 28–43% of truck-kilometres run empty.
findings.detail:
NITI Aayog and RMI (June 2021) figures:
- Road freight costs ₹3.679 per tonne-km, against ₹1.678 for rail. 71% of India's freight goes by road.
- Indian trucks cover 250–400 km a day, against 700–800 km in the US and Europe.
- They run empty for 28–43% of the distance and are often overloaded.

The report names digital load matching, with Porter as its example, as a way to cut empty running. Rough example: a 9 t yard-to-recycler load over 150 km costs about ₹5,000 (₹0.55/kg). That is more than a quarter of the ₹2/kg margin a Bengaluru dealer reported. Filling trucks and finding return loads matters more than saving kilometres.

findings.point: E-way bills matter mainly for metal-heavy or bulk loads. Handcarts, cycles and short trips to a weighbridge are exempt.
findings.detail:
Rules under CGST Rule 138:
- An e-way bill is needed before moving goods worth more than ₹50,000.
- When a registered buyer (a yard) buys from an unregistered seller (a kabadiwala) and is known when the goods set off, the buyer generates it. Unregistered persons can enrol (Form ENR-03) to generate one themselves.
- Not needed for non-motorised transport (handcart, cycle-cart), or for a trip of up to 20 km to a weighbridge and back with a delivery challan.
- Vehicle details (Part B) can be skipped for moves of up to 50 km to a transporter.
- Validity is one day per 200 km, and e-way bills can be generated by SMS.

Karnataka's intra-state threshold is ₹50,000, half the ₹1 lakh used in Tamil Nadu, Maharashtra and Delhi (ClearTax). At Bengaluru door prices, a full 750 kg Tata Ace of newspaper is worth about ₹7,500 and of iron about ₹16,500. But 100 kg of copper (₹500/kg) or about 330 kg of aluminium (₹150/kg) already reaches ₹50,000.

findings.point: Since 10 October 2024, a registered yard that buys metal scrap from an unregistered kabadiwala pays the GST itself (reverse charge).
findings.detail: Notification 6/2024-Central Tax (Rate), dated 8 Oct 2024, applies reverse charge to metal scrap in Customs Tariff chapters 72–81 sold by an unregistered person to a registered one, from 10 Oct 2024. Notification 25/2024-Central Tax, from the same date, adds tax deduction at source when registered buyers take metal scrap from registered sellers. For its own invoice and any e-way bill, the yard needs the seller's name and address, the material, weight, rate and vehicle. Luma.Green's hand-off record can carry exactly these fields, so the yard doesn't have to type them in again.

findings.point: Every scale used in trade needs a valid Legal Metrology stamp, and expired stamps are a common violation in Karnataka.
findings.detail:
Rule 27 of the Legal Metrology (General) Rules, 2011 sets re-verification every 24 months for weights and beam scales, and every 12 months for other instruments, which covers electronic platform scales and weighbridges. Invest Karnataka's penalty list (Sep 2025):
- ₹2,000–10,000 for using an unverified weight (s.33)
- up to ₹50,000 for tampering (s.26)
- up to ₹1 lakh for non-standard weights (s.25)
- jail for repeat offences

In the 17 months to August 2024, Karnataka's Legal Metrology department ran 20,391 inspections, booked 5,375 cases and collected ₹1.79 crore. Not renewing the stamp was a common violation, and iron and steel were among the trades named (News Karnataka, 6 Nov 2024).

findings.point: Credit standards and B2B buyers expect a weight record when material leaves and when it arrives, tied to documents.
findings.detail: Verra's plastic collection methodology (PWRM0001 v1.1) requires the dry weight to be recorded every time material leaves a collection site. It is measured at the site, the destination, or both, and cross-checked with invoices, payment receipts or goods receipt notes. Weighbridges must be calibrated to the maker's specification or at least every 3 years. Recykal.Market, a B2B scrap marketplace, gives each trade an invoice, e-way bill and weight certificate. It syncs weighbridge slips and quality checks at the buyer's gate and offers live GPS tracking with ETA and driver contact. At minimum, each Luma.Green hand-off needs a photo of the weighbridge slip plus gross, tare and net weights before its records are usable for EPR and credits.

findings.point: The Solid Waste Management Rules 2026 (in force 1 April 2026) add registration, returns, tracked vehicles and PPE for anyone collecting and transporting waste on a city's behalf.
findings.detail:
Rule 8 applies to the local body and any contractor or third party it authorises. They must:
- register on CPCB's central portal
- hand waste only to registered facilities
- file quarterly returns (by the 15th of the month after each quarter) and annual returns (by 30 June), listing quantities by generator and by receiving facility
- use vehicles with separate compartments
- give workers PPE and training
- fit collection vehicles with tracking devices in cities of over 50,000 people

Bulk waste generators (100 kg of waste a day, 20,000 m² of floor area, or 40,000 litres of water a day) must register and must not deal with unregistered entities (Rule 6). The rules count waste traders as 'informal waste collectors', which cities must bring into the system. If Luma.Green's kabadiwalas serve apartment societies or offices, they may need this registration. Luma.Green's records could produce the returns.

findings.point: Bengaluru bans goods vehicles from key elevated roads for weeks at a time, by vehicle type and hour.
findings.detail:
Bengaluru Traffic Police notices for September 2026 (read from the Kannada notices on its site):
- Electronic City elevated tollway (11–30 Sep): goods autos banned all day, other goods vehicles 6 am–10 pm.
- Airport Road flyover: all commercial goods vehicles barred 6 am–10 pm.
- BGS flyover and the Silk Board–Ragigudda double-decker: heavy goods vehicles barred round the clock. On BGS, other goods vehicles are also kept off 7–11 am and 4–10 pm.
- Peenya elevated corridor (4–30 Sep): goods autos barred all day.

The reasons given are repairs, road resurfacing and load tests, so the bans change month to month. Routing services won't know about them. A small table the admin updates is the simple answer.

findings.point: Route suggestions are cheap: Mapbox, already planned, orders up to 12 stops per request and is free for the first 100,000 requests a month.
findings.detail: Mapbox's Optimization API v1 takes 2–12 locations and supports pickup-and-drop-off pairs (up to 25) and 300 requests a minute. It has no time windows or vehicle capacities; those are in the v2 beta. Optimization, Directions and Matrix are each free for the first 100,000 requests (or elements) a month, then $2.00 per 1,000. For pooled yard collections with capacities and time windows, VROOM, a free open-source engine (BSD-2 licence), solves these problems in milliseconds. It runs on OSRM, Valhalla or Openrouteservice, so no paid route optimiser is needed until volumes justify it.

findings.point: Freight for bulk loads is already a partner market. Luma.Green should own the data, not the trucks.
findings.detail: Porter lists Bengaluru vehicles from a 350 kg e-loader up to the Tata 407 for heavy goods, charged per km. Vahak claims 10 lakh+ transporters and lorry owners, with load posting, bidding, full and part loads, and live tracking. Recykal Express finds vetted transporters at short notice, with live GPS, ETA alerts and driver contact. NITI Aayog points to digital load matching as the fix for empty trucks. Building a fleet or a trucking marketplace would be costly and isn't Luma.Green's strength. A freight estimate from an editable rate table, plus a hand-off to the transporter the yard already uses, shows investors the full flow at almost no cost.

findings.point: Karnataka charges platforms a 1% welfare fee on gig payouts, capped per transaction by vehicle type.
findings.detail: From 13 Feb 2026, platforms in ride-hailing, delivery, logistics and e-marketplaces pay 1% of each gig payout. The cap per transaction is ₹0.50 for two-wheelers, ₹0.75 for three-wheelers, ₹1.00 for light commercial vehicles and ₹1.50 for heavy ones. The platform pays, not the worker, and declares it quarterly (SCC Online, 18 Feb 2026). If Saathis take pickups through Luma.Green, the sums are tiny. But Luma.Green would have to record the vehicle type and payout of every job, and may have to register as an aggregator.

findings.point: Batteries and other special-care waste need an authorised transporter and paperwork, not a kabadiwala's auto.
findings.detail:
CPCB's July 2026 guidelines for waste batteries require:
- lithium-ion packs moved at under 30% charge, with terminals taped
- lead-acid batteries upright in sealed, acid-resistant containers, on leak-proof floors lined with sawdust
- a fire extinguisher in the vehicle
- the State Pollution Control Board told in advance, with a manifest under the Hazardous Waste Rules 2016
- no-objection certificates from both states for inter-state transit

The household flow should flag batteries and e-waste and send them to authorised collectors, not mix them into dry-scrap pickups.

recommendations.feature: Pickup time slots with a limit per kabadiwala, plus a minimum load
recommendations.why: Missed and late pickups are where household apps fail, and each pickup takes 45–60 minutes. Offer 2-hour windows. Each kabadiwala sets how many pickups fit in a window (default 2 per vehicle), and full windows disappear. If the AI estimate is under the admin's minimum (default 15 kg, as The Kabadiwala uses), suggest a drop-off with the shop code instead. All these numbers live in one admin-editable serviceRules table with start dates, like the price tables.

recommendations.feature: Today's route for the kabadiwala, and 'on the way' with an ETA for the household
recommendations.why: Mapbox is already planned. Its Optimization API v1 orders up to 12 stops per call and is free for the first 100,000 calls a month. One button orders the day's accepted pickups and opens navigation. While the kabadiwala is on the way, the tracking page shows an ETA from his phone; location sharing stops once the pickup is done. A strong demo for little code.

recommendations.feature: Vehicle fit from the photo estimate
recommendations.why: Scrapr already makes households pick a vehicle for their load; Luma.Green can do it automatically. It matches the estimated kg and bulk (loose or bundled) to a handcart, cycle, auto or mini-truck, using an editable vehicleTypes table (payload kg, rough volume, fares). Only kabadiwalas whose registered vehicle fits are offered, and heavy lots never go to a handcart.

recommendations.feature: Pooled yard collection: fill one vehicle from several nearby kabadiwalas
recommendations.why: This is the hand-off the founder called most important. The yard sees nearby stock on a map and picks shops until a capacity bar for the chosen vehicle (kg and volume) is full. It gets a suggested stop order and collection window, and each kabadiwala accepts or declines. A 'yard collects / kabadiwala delivers' switch and a 'who pays freight' field cover both patterns seen in Bengaluru. Pooling tackles empty running (28–43%) and light materials that fill a vehicle by volume. This answers questions 4, 5 and 9 in docs/product/kabadiwala-to-yard.md.

recommendations.feature: Freight estimate from an admin rate table, booked with the yard's own transporter or a partner
recommendations.why: Porter publishes only starting fares (₹150–330 in Bengaluru) and no public API. So keep an editable fare per vehicle type (base fare, ₹/km, loading charge) and show an estimate per load and per kg. Booking stays with the yard's usual transporter or a partner app. A real partner integration waits until volumes justify it.

recommendations.feature: Weight slip when a load leaves and when it arrives, for every business hand-off
recommendations.why: Record the kabadiwala's weight when the load leaves and the yard's weight on arrival (weighbridge or platform scale). Add a slip photo, the vehicle number, gross, tare and net weights, and a deduction line with a reason. Flag gaps above an editable tolerance. Also store each scale's Legal Metrology stamp expiry and send a reminder 30 days before its yearly re-verification. Verra, EPR buyers and Recykal-style document packs expect this, and it heads off weight disputes.

recommendations.feature: Paperwork checklist for each load (delivery challan, e-way bill, reverse charge)
recommendations.why: From the load's value, vehicle and material, tell each side what the law expects. A handcart, or a weighbridge trip of up to 20 km with a delivery challan, needs no e-way bill. Above ₹50,000 in Karnataka an e-way bill is needed, and the registered buyer generates it when buying from an unregistered kabadiwala. Metal scrap bought from unregistered sellers carries reverse-charge GST. Keep these rules in an admin table by state with start dates, and export the fields. Filing stays in the yard's GST software or with a GST filing provider later.

recommendations.feature: Vehicle, driver and live status for each bulk load
recommendations.why: Capture the vehicle number and driver's phone at booking and a photo at loading. Share the phone's location only while the load is moving. Statuses run scheduled → loading → on the way → weighed on arrival. Recykal sells this (GPS, ETA, driver contact); Luma.Green can do a simple version without tracking hardware. The SWM Rules 2026 already require tracked vehicles for city collection contracts.

recommendations.feature: Admin-edited road restrictions and safe loading rules
recommendations.why: Bengaluru's September 2026 notices bar goods vehicles from several elevated roads by vehicle type and hour, and routing services don't know this. A small roadRestrictions table (road, vehicle types, hours, start and end dates, source link) warns when a collection window clashes. Add a loading checklist: never plan beyond the vehicle's rated payload, cover open loads, gloves and shoes for loaders.

recommendations.feature: Guardrail for special-care waste (batteries, e-waste)
recommendations.why: Batteries need authorised transport under CPCB's 2026 guidelines: charge limits, sealed containers, advance notice to the pollution board, manifests. Tag these materials in the catalogue, keep them out of normal pickups, and point households to authorised collectors or brand take-back points.

recommendations.feature: Route planning across several vehicles, and partner freight for yard-to-recycler loads
recommendations.why: Once yards run several vehicles a day, move from Mapbox v1 to VROOM, a free open-source engine on our own server (BSD-2 licence) that handles time windows and capacities. Connect a freight partner for full-truck loads (Porter within the city, Vahak-style load boards between cities). Luma.Green keeps the weights, documents and trail; partners own the trucks and drivers.

recommendations.feature: Compliance exports: SWM Rules 2026 returns and gig welfare-fee reports
recommendations.why: When kabadiwalas serve bulk generators or Saathis do paid pickups, the same records can produce two reports. One is the quarterly SWM return (quantity per generator and per receiving facility). The other is Karnataka's quarterly welfare-fee declaration (payout and vehicle type per job). Build them as exports once the obligations are confirmed.

| 8 | Freight estimate | Yard, kabadiwala, recycler | Estimate per load and per kg from base fare + ₹/km + loading; booked with the yard's own transporter or a partner | Build the data; partner makes the trip | `vehicleTypes` | Prototype now |
| 9 | Weight slip when a load leaves and when it arrives | Kabadiwala, yard, recycler | Leaving vs arriving weight, slip photo, gross/tare/net, deduction reason, flag when the gap is too big | Build | `serviceRules.weightTolerance` | Pilot |

All thresholds, fares and restrictions live in admin-editable Convex tables with an `effectiveFrom` date, like the price tables (ADR 0008). Money is stored in paise and mass in grams.
risks: Kabadiwalas may find household pickups not worth it (45–60 minutes each), then skip small bookings. No-shows are the main complaint about existing apps. Minimum loads, drop-off as the default, and limits per slot reduce the risk but don't remove it.

If Luma.Green books vehicles or dispatches Saathis, it may count as an aggregator under Karnataka's gig-workers law (1% fee, quarterly declarations). It could also be drawn into accident or damage claims. Keep transport contracts between the parties and their transporters.

The paperwork checklist could be wrong or go out of date: e-way bill thresholds, reverse charge on metal scrap, state rules. Users could then face penalties. Label it as guidance, keep the rules in dated admin tables, and have a chartered accountant review them before the pilot.
Recording weights at both ends will surface gaps from moisture, contamination and scale error. Without an agreed tolerance and deduction reasons, the numbers can create disputes instead of trust.
Temporary road bans and lane-level access in Bengaluru aren't in routing services, so promise time windows, not exact times.
Porter and other freight apps publish only starting fares and no public API. Freight estimates will be rough until pilot yards share real per-km charges.
Safety: lithium-battery fires, lifting injuries, overloaded vehicles, and Saathis entering homes. The SWM Rules 2026 expect PPE and training for collection and transport workers.
Location privacy: kabadiwala and driver locations must be shared only during an active job and deleted after, in line with the data-protection page.
openQuestions: In Bengaluru, do yards usually collect with their own vehicles or do kabadiwalas deliver? Who pays the freight? (Ask pilot yards.)
What do pilot yards and local transporters actually charge per km and for loading? Porter publishes only starting fares.
What is the smallest load per material worth a yard collection, by kg and by volume?
Will yards generate e-way bills in their own GST software, or does Luma.Green need a GST filing partner? Is the SMS e-way bill enough for small yards?

Will the Greater Bengaluru Authority require kabadiwalas, or Luma.Green, to register under the SWM Rules 2026 before collecting from bulk generators (e.g. apartment societies producing over 100 kg a day)?
Is Luma.Green an 'aggregator' under Karnataka's gig-workers law if Saathis do pickups but are paid by kabadiwalas?
Have the Legal Metrology penalties listed by Invest Karnataka (Sep 2025) changed since?
Can a startup use ULIP, the government's logistics data platform (vehicle records, driving licences, FASTag data), to check transporters' vehicles and drivers? Not checked in this research.
What are Bengaluru's standing, city-wide entry hours for goods vehicles? Only the temporary September 2026 notices were checked.
