result.headline: About 1 in 5 Indian adults cannot read (78.2% adult literacy, 2024) and 88% of India's mobile browsing is Chrome on Android, so Luma.Green's field screens must lead with pictures, numbers and voice. Yet 34 of the app's 51 buttons are only 28–36 px tall against its own 44–56 px rule, and the same rupee amount appears in five different formats across its 12 languages.

findings.point: Low literacy is the main design case, and text-first screens fail these users
findings.detail: The World Bank (UNESCO data) puts India's adult literacy at 78.16% in 2024. That means about one adult in five cannot read, and many more read slowly. Microsoft Research India ran a study (Medhi Thies et al., ACM TOCHI, April 2011) in two parts: field research with 90 low-literacy people in India, Kenya, the Philippines and South Africa, then tests with 70+ Indian participants. Text interfaces could not be used by first-time low-literacy users, and literate beginners made many errors with them. A picture-based interface gave the best task completion for mobile banking, and a live phone operator was up to 10 times more accurate than text for data entry. VideoKheti (CHI 2013, 20 farmers) combined speech, pictures and touch, but success still depended on how much schooling users had. Screen design alone will not reach everyone, so a person who helps has to be part of the design.

findings.point: In Bengaluru, people often use phones through a helper, and many phones are shared
findings.detail: Sambasivan, Cutrell, Toyama and Nardi (CHI 2010) studied two Bangalore slums and describe three ways a helper steps in: typing in the request, reading the answer aloud, or doing the whole task. Google researchers Sambasivan and Checkley (SOUPS 2018, winner of a privacy award) found that women in India, Pakistan and Bangladesh share phones with family. They protect their privacy with app locks, by deleting content, by avoiding some apps and by using private modes. This supports the current no-account household flow. It also argues for letting a kabadiwala or Saathi book on someone's behalf, keeping SMS tracking links low on personal detail, and not leaving personal data on screen.

findings.point: Use few words, keep labels visible, one column, and no scrolling before the main decision
findings.detail: NN/g's study of lower-literacy readers (2005) found they read word by word, look at a narrow area of the page, lose their place when they scroll, and take the first answer that seems right. Simpler pages raised their task completion by 135% and helped strong readers too. NN/g's advice: grade-6 reading level on key pages, one column, no moving text, and simple step-by-step navigation. NN/g's icon study (2014) found only a few icons are understood everywhere (home, print, search). Labels should always be visible, and if no icon comes to mind within 5 seconds, use a word. Google's Next Billion Users site now redirects to the Google blog (checked 29 Sep 2026). Its developer advice lives on as Android's Build for Billions guidelines, which ask for icons that low-literacy users understand, numbers and dates in local formats, and right-to-left support.

findings.point: The project's rule of 44 px buttons (48–56 px for main actions) is right, but most buttons don't meet it
findings.detail: The accessibility standard WCAG 2.2 sets 24x24 CSS px as the minimum at level AA and 44x44 at the stricter level AAA, pointing to users with shaky hands or on the move. Google recommends 48x48 dp (about 9 mm) with 8 dp gaps. The shadcn Button in the repo is 32 px tall by default, 36 px at size lg, 28 px at size sm and 36 px at size icon-lg. Of the 51 Button uses outside components/ui, 34 use those default sizes. Only 17 are set by hand to 44–48 px. In the phone-first areas (join, auth, app, public site), 18 of 35 buttons are 28–36 px.

findings.point: Two current colour settings fail accessibility contrast rules where the layout uses them
findings.detail: We computed contrast ratios from the colour values in src/app/globals.css using the standard WCAG formula. Grey helper text (--muted-foreground) on the grey page background (--muted) is 4.34:1, below the 4.5:1 minimum for text; on white cards it is 4.73:1, which passes. Input and card borders (--input, --border) are 1.26:1 on white. WCAG asks for 3:1 on the outline that shows where a control is, so input boxes almost disappear, and sunlight makes it worse. The two lightest chart greens are 1.68:1 and 2.35:1 on white; chart graphics need 3:1. The brand green passes (5.71:1 on white, 5.47:1 for white text on it). Darkening the helper grey to oklch(0.50 0 0) gives 5.5:1 on the grey page, and oklch(0.64 0 0) for input borders gives 3.36:1. WCAG also says colour must never be the only signal, so every material colour needs its icon and name.

findings.point: The same rupee amount appears in five different formats across the 12 languages
findings.detail: The app's formatting helper (useFormat in src/components/app/format.ts) formats numbers in the page's language. We checked the output in Node 24, which uses the same locale data as Chrome. One lakh twenty-five thousand rupees shows as ₹125,000 in English, Kannada, Malayalam and Urdu, and as ₹1,25,000 in Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, Gujarati and Punjabi. Bengali shows ১,২৫,০০০₹ (Bengali digits, symbol after). Marathi shows ₹१२५,००० (Devanagari digits, Western grouping). Arabic shows 125,000 ₹. The English demo investors will see has no lakh grouping. Article 343(1) of the Constitution makes international numerals (1, 2, 3) the official form. Formatting every price, weight and payout with Indian (lakh) grouping and international digits gives one format everywhere while the words stay translated.

findings.point: The typical user has Chrome on a 360-px-wide Android phone and an uneven network
findings.detail: StatCounter, India mobile, August 2026: Android 92.79%, iOS 7.15%. Chrome has 88.13% of browsing, then Opera 4.88%, Safari 3.97% and UC 1.67%. The most common screen is 360x800 (18.46%); 360-px-wide screens make up about 23% and 393-px-wide about 12.5%. Alex Russell's 2024 performance budget assumes a mid-range phone like a Galaxy A51 on a 7.2 Mbps connection. To be usable within 3 seconds, a JavaScript-heavy site can load about 365 KB of compressed JavaScript (730 KB in total); a mostly-HTML site can load about 75 KB of JavaScript. He notes India's average speeds are rising fast but vary enormously. Google's Build for Billions adds: work offline first, lower image quality on slow connections, use the WebP image format, let users control data use, and support phones with little memory (Android Go targets phones with 4 GB or less).

findings.point: Next.js 16.3 has offline helpers, but the app manifest lacks the icons Chrome needs to install it
findings.detail: The Next.js guide to installable web apps (version 16.3.6, updated 30 Jul 2026) covers the manifest and push notifications, and says the install prompt does not need offline support. It points to a new useOffline hook, which detects loss of connection and retries failed page loads and form actions automatically. Next marks it experimental and not yet for production. For full offline caching it points to the Serwist library. Chrome offers to install an app only if the manifest has 192 px and 512 px icons, a name, a start page and a display mode, and only after the user taps once and stays 30 seconds. Screenshots and a description give a richer install screen. Luma.Green's manifest lists only /logo.svg. Background Sync, which sends saved work once the network returns, works only in Chrome and Edge: acceptable with 88% Chrome, but other browsers need a fallback.

findings.point: Sign-in codes can fill in automatically if the SMS template has one extra line
findings.detail: Chrome on Android reads the code from the SMS automatically (the WebOTP feature) when the last line is '@luma.green #123456'; it needs HTTPS and works only on that domain. Safari offers the code using the input's autocomplete='one-time-code' setting alone. The code inputs (src/components/auth/verify-flow.tsx) already have that setting. But the code template drafted in docs/operations/services.md has no domain line. Under the telecom DLT rules, every SMS must match its approved template exactly, per language. So the line has to be added before the founder's DLT registration is approved, or the templates will need approving again later.

findings.point: Spoken prompts are possible in all 12 languages today
findings.detail: Browsers can speak text and recognise speech through the Web Speech API. Chrome sends speech to a server for recognition by default, with an on-device option. But which voices a phone has varies. Recording the audio ahead of time avoids that. Google Cloud's Chirp 3 HD voices are fully released for Bengali, Gujarati, Hindi, Kannada, Malayalam, Marathi, Tamil, Telugu, Urdu, Indian English and Arabic, with Punjabi in preview. That covers every Luma.Green language. The free, open-source Indic Parler-TTS (AI4Bharat and Hugging Face, Apache 2.0 licence, 69 voices) officially supports 20 languages including Kannada, Tamil, Telugu, Urdu and Hindi, but not Punjabi or Arabic. Project Vaani (IISc Bengaluru, ARTPARK, Google) has released 31,278 hours of speech from 156,208 speakers in 105 languages under an open CC BY 4.0 licence, useful later for voice input that handles dialects. The kabadiwala spec already asks for a speaker button.

findings.point: The Bengaluru pilot needs Tamil, Telugu and Urdu (right-to-left), not only Kannada, Hindi and English
findings.detail: Census 2011 mother tongues in Bengaluru: Kannada 42.05%, Tamil 16.34%, Telugu 13.73%, Urdu 13.00%, Hindi 4.64%. docs/product/vision.md names Kannada, Hindi and English as the pilot's main languages, which leaves the first language of about 43% of residents as secondary. Urdu reads right to left, so mirrored layouts, arrow icons and numbers inside Urdu text need testing before the pilot. Kannada and Malayalam also show amounts with Western digit grouping (see the finding on number formats).

findings.point: Only public-domain (CC0) kits come with no conditions; most free illustration libraries have strings attached
findings.detail: No credit needed and free to edit: Open Peeps (CC0, 584,688 mix-and-match combinations), Humaaans (CC0), Open Doodles (CC0), Healthicons (CC0, filled and outline icons at 24 and 48 px) and the older illlustrations set (CC0). Free but with limits: unDraw (no credit needed, but no redistributing, no competing service, no use to train AI), ManyPixels (20,000+ images, no credit needed, no redistributing), and DrawKit (no credit needed, but no redistributing, templates, merchandise or AI training). Credit required: Storyset on the free plan (a paid Flaticon Premium subscription removes it), free Noun Project icons (CC BY 3.0; a paid licence removes it), Twemoji (CC BY 4.0), and OpenMoji (CC BY-SA 4.0, so any edited emoji must be shared under the same licence). Icons: Lucide (ISC licence, already in the repo) and Google's Material Symbols (Apache 2.0, credit optional, adjustable fill and weight; includes recycling, scale, currency_rupee, water_bottle and forklift).

findings.point: Open artwork that shows Indian life is scarce, and the obvious sources have licence traps
findings.detail: UX4G 3.0, the Government of India design system from NeGD (MeitY), says it is free for government departments and their websites, and gives no permission for private products. Figma Community files under Figma's Community Free Resource License cannot be edited into new work or used by third parties, so Indian illustration packs found there cannot simply be shipped. StoryWeaver (Pratham Books: about 34,000 openly licensed books in about 300 languages, Creative Commons 4.0) is the richest open source of Indian daily-life art, but styles vary and each image needs a credit. On Wikimedia Commons the licence varies per file, and photos of identifiable people need their consent. Unsplash and Pixabay need no credit but forbid building a competing image service and misusing photos of recognisable people. IconScout, Blush and Icons8 blocked our access (HTTP 403), so their terms are unverified.

findings.point: The shadcn/Tailwind setup is easy to extend, but the planned material colours aren't built yet
findings.detail: shadcn pairs each background colour with a text colour (the -foreground token), defines colours in the OKLCH format, and adds new ones in two short CSS steps (its example adds a warning colour). One radius setting drives all corner sizes. The shadcn registry can share components, hooks, settings and colours between projects, installed with one CLI command. docs/architecture/frontend.md plans colours for paper, cardboard, plastic, metal, glass and e-waste, but globals.css doesn't define them yet. Nothing in the code enforces the rule of one icon and one colour per material.

recommendations.feature: Larger button sizes for phone screens
recommendations.why: 34 of 51 buttons are 28–36 px, below the project's own 44/48–56 px rule and Google's 48 dp. Add three sizes to the shared Button: touch (48 px), action (56 px, larger text, icon plus label) and icon-touch (48 px square). Make them the default in the household, kabadiwala, Saathi and join screens. Admin can keep shadcn's defaults, which already meet the WCAG AA minimum of 24 px.

recommendations.feature: One number format everywhere: lakh grouping with international digits
recommendations.why: Today one amount appears in five formats across the locales, and the English demo shows ₹125,000 instead of ₹1,25,000. Change useFormat() to format money, weights and counts with Indian (lakh) grouping and international digits, keeping the words translated. Mark amounts as left-to-right inside Urdu and Arabic text, and add a unit test per language. This matches Article 343's official numerals. Check the choice with Bengali and Marathi users in the pilot.

recommendations.feature: Fix failing colours, add material colours, and test contrast automatically
recommendations.why: Set the grey helper text to oklch(0.50 0 0) (5.5:1 on the grey page) and input borders to oklch(0.64 0 0) (3.36:1), and darken the lightest chart greens. Add a colour and matching text colour for each material (paper, cardboard, plastic, metal, glass, e-waste), plus success, warning and info colours. Add a unit test that fails if any text colour pair is below 4.5:1 or any icon or border pair is below 3:1. Materials should differ in lightness as well as hue, and always show an icon and a name.

recommendations.feature: A small set of shared building blocks for low-literacy screens
recommendations.why: Build these from existing shadcn pieces: MaterialTile (photo or picture, colour, and a 1–2 word name), IconAction (icon with a label that is always visible), QuantityStepper (plus and minus in half-kilo steps, with a big number keypad instead of free typing), MoneyAmount (large, evenly spaced digits), ListenButton, and OfflineBanner (using Next's useOffline). Keep one fixed main button at the bottom of each screen. Store labels, icon names, colours, photo ids and audio per language in one data table, so the founders can change them without code.

recommendations.feature: Illustration kit: Open Peeps plus commissioned Indian clothing and props
recommendations.why: Open Peeps is public domain (CC0): no credits, free to edit, and none of unDraw's or DrawKit's limits on redistribution or AI use. Commission about 20–30 extra pieces in the same line style: kurta, saree, salwar with dupatta, lungi or mundu, caps, turbans, hijab and a Saathi vest, plus a pushcart (thela), tricycle cart, platform scale, sacks, newspaper bundles, cardboard bales, PET bottles, a tempo or auto, and a warehouse shed. Recolour them with CSS variables, compress each SVG, and keep a credits file (source, licence, link, date checked). Use unDraw only on the public site. Keep Storyset (free plan), free Noun Project icons and OpenMoji out of the app.

recommendations.feature: A 'Hear it' button with pre-recorded audio for the demo's key screens
recommendations.why: Text screens fail first-time low-literacy users; voice plus pictures helps. Generate 10–20 prompts (how to sell, photo tips, the estimate, booking, accept or reject, weigh and pay) in Kannada, Hindi and English, using Google's Chirp 3 HD voices or the free Indic Parler-TTS. Store them as small audio files per message and language, cached on the phone. Have native speakers check how trade words like raddi and bhangar are pronounced. For the pilot, cover every prompt in every pilot language, and speak live details (weights, times, areas) with text-to-speech on the fly.

recommendations.feature: Automatic code fill-in for every code SMS
recommendations.why: Add '@luma.green #{#var#}' as the last line of the sign-in and booking code template in every language before DLT approval. On the verify screen, ask Chrome for Android to read the code, and keep the existing one-time-code setting for iPhones. This removes typing six digits, which is error-prone for new smartphone users. Check that the extra line does not push Kannada or Hindi templates into a second SMS segment.

recommendations.feature: Installable app that copes with dropped connections
recommendations.why: Add 192 px and 512 px PNG icons, adaptive (maskable) icons, screenshots, a description and home-screen shortcuts ('Sell scrap', 'Today') to manifest.ts, and ask kabadiwalas to install once. Try Next's experimental offline detection and retries in preview first. Then add Serwist for offline screens and cached audio and pictures, plus a local queue for weigh-and-pay records: send in the background on Chrome, or on next open in other browsers. A weighing must never be lost.

recommendations.feature: Assisted mode: 'Book for someone' and 'Call me'
recommendations.why: People in Bangalore slums often use phones through a helper (CHI 2010), and a live operator was up to 10 times more accurate than text (TOCHI 2011). Let a kabadiwala or Saathi book a pickup for a household, which the household confirms with its SMS code. Add a 'Call me' button that reaches the admin during the pilot.

recommendations.feature: Bengaluru language testing, including Urdu (right-to-left), plus a picture recognition test
recommendations.why: Bengaluru is 42% Kannada, 16% Tamil, 14% Telugu and 13% Urdu speakers. Test the core flows in all four plus Hindi and English with native speakers. Check that line spacing doesn't clip Indian scripts, that arrows mirror in Urdu, and how numbers sit inside Urdu text. Before fixing the material pictures, run a quick test with 5 users to check they recognise each one.

recommendations.feature: Automatic accessibility and page-weight checks in CI
recommendations.why: Add automated accessibility checks (axe) to the Playwright end-to-end tests at 360x800, the most common Indian screen, and fail the build on contrast, button-size or missing-label errors. Keep household and kabadiwala pages under about 365 KB of compressed JavaScript, the 3-second budget on a mid-range phone, and serve images as WebP or AVIF.

recommendations.feature: Publish a Luma.Green design kit and an open set of material pictures
recommendations.why: Package the colours, the low-literacy building blocks and an openly licensed set of material pictures as a shadcn registry. Partner yards, recyclers, manufacturers and a future mobile app can then reuse the same icons, colours and words, which is the practical way for the industry to adopt Luma.Green's conventions. Add voice input later (on-device recognition where available, then dialect models trained on Vaani-style data).

result.artifactMarkdown:
## Illustration and icon sources for Luma.Green (licences checked 29 Sep 2026)

Rule of thumb: prefer public-domain (CC0) or credit-free licences for anything that ships inside the app, keep attribution-required art to the pitch deck or a credits page, and record every asset in a credits file (source, licence, link, date checked).

| Source | What it is | Licence | Attribution rule | Fit for Indian context | Recommendation |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [Open Peeps](https://www.openpeeps.com/) (Pablo Stanley) | Hand-drawn people kit, 584,688 mix-and-match combinations, recolourable | CC0 | None (credit appreciated) | Medium: neutral line style; no Indian clothing yet, but parts can be added | **Adopt** as the base people kit; commission Indian clothing and props in the same style |
| [Humaaans](https://www.humaaans.com/) | Flat people kit (hair, tops, trousers swappable) | CC0 | None | Medium: same clothing gap | Backup base; never mix with Open Peeps on one screen |
| [Open Doodles](https://www.opendoodles.com/) | Sketch scenes (SVG, PNG, GIF) | CC0 | None | Low | Empty-screen art that matches Open Peeps |
| [illlustrations](https://illlustrations.co/license) (realvjy) | 120+ scenes | Older open set CC0; newer premium and builder assets under other terms | None for the CC0 set | Low–Medium | Optional; confirm each file is from the CC0 set |
| [Healthicons](https://healthicons.org/) | Filled and outline pictograms, 24/48 px: people, jobs, money, phones, vehicles | CC0 | None | Medium: made for public-health messaging | **Use** for people and job pictures on tiles |
| [unDraw](https://undraw.co/license) | Flat scenes with one recolourable accent | Own licence: free for commercial use and edits; no redistributing, competing services, scraping, or AI training | None | Low: office and tech scenes | Public site and empty screens only; never feed into AI image tools |
| [ManyPixels](https://www.manypixels.co/gallery) | 20,000+ illustrations, 5 styles, colour filter | Free for commercial and non-commercial use; no redistributing or competing service | None | Low–Medium | Marketing pages only (styles may clash) |
| [DrawKit](https://www.drawkit.com/license) | Free and premium illustration and icon packs | Commercial use allowed; no redistributing, sub-licensing, templates, merchandise or AI training | None (appreciated) | Low | Optional |
| [Storyset](https://storyset.com/terms) (Freepik) | Editable and animated scenes, 5 styles | Free only with credit; Flaticon Premium removes the credit; no resale or logos | Credit Storyset wherever used (free plan) | Medium: large catalogue with some Indian scenes | Pitch deck only, or pay; keep out of the app on the free plan |
| [Noun Project](https://thenounproject.com/legal/terms-of-use/) | Icons and photos | Free = CC BY 3.0; a paid royalty-free licence removes the credit | Credit each icon's creator (free use) | High for uncommon Indian objects (search one by one) | Buy the licence if any icon ships in the app |
| [StoryWeaver / Pratham Books](https://prathambooks.org/) | Art from about 34,000 open picture books in about 300 languages | Creative Commons 4.0 (check each image) | Illustrator, licence and link for each image | **High**: Indian homes, streets and work, drawn by Indian illustrators | Best open art of Indian daily life for onboarding and stories; styles vary |
| [UX4G 3.0](https://www.ux4g.gov.in/) (NeGD, MeitY) | Government of India design system, icons, Figma kit, npm package | Free for government departments and their websites; no permission for private products | n/a | High: Indian public-service patterns | Reference only; ask NeGD before reusing assets |
| [Figma Community packs](https://www.figma.com/legal/community-free-resource-license/) | Indian illustration kits and more | Files under Figma's Community Free Resource License: no editing into new work, no use by third parties | Per file | Varies | Don't ship without the creator's written permission |
| [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/Commons:Reusing_content_outside_Wikimedia) | Real photos of India's scrap trade | Per file: CC BY, CC BY-SA or public domain; consent needed for identifiable people | Author, licence and link; edited versions of CC BY-SA files must stay CC BY-SA | High | Research and reference; ship only CC BY or public-domain files, credited |
| [Unsplash](https://unsplash.com/license) | Photos, many from India | Free for commercial use; no selling unedited copies; no competing service | Not required | Medium–High | Public site and onboarding; prefer your own photos for materials |
| [Pixabay](https://pixabay.com/service/license-summary/) | Photos and vectors | Free; no reselling as-is; no trademark use; care with recognisable people | Not required | Medium | Same as Unsplash |
| [Lucide](https://lucide.dev/license) (in repo, v1.48.0) | UI line icons, including indian-rupee, recycle, scale, weight, truck, newspaper, battery, forklift, mic, volume-2 | ISC; about 100 icons taken from Feather are MIT | Keep the licence text with the code; no on-screen credit | Low–Medium | **Keep** as the only UI icon set; always show a label |
| [Material Symbols](https://github.com/google/material-design-icons) | Adjustable icons (fill, weight, grade, size); includes recycling, scale, currency_rupee, water_bottle, forklift, solar_power | Apache 2.0 | Optional (an About-screen credit is appreciated) | Medium | Only for filled tiles where Lucide has no icon; import individual SVGs, not the full font |
| [Noto Emoji](https://github.com/googlefonts/noto-emoji) | Colour and monochrome emoji | Fonts OFL 1.1; images and tools Apache 2.0; flags public domain | Keep the licence notice | Medium–High: objects familiar from WhatsApp (newspaper, package, bottle, tin can, battery, phone, T-shirt) | Quick material pictures; bundle the SVGs so every phone looks the same |
| [Fluent Emoji](https://github.com/microsoft/fluentui-emoji) (Microsoft) | 3D, colour and flat emoji | MIT | Keep the licence notice | Medium–High | Alternative to Noto (warmer 3D look) |
| [Twemoji](https://github.com/jdecked/twemoji) (community fork) | Emoji up to Unicode 17 | Graphics CC BY 4.0; code MIT | Credit in the README, About screen or footer | Medium–High | Fine with a credits page |
| [OpenMoji](https://openmoji.org/faq/) | Open emoji and extra icons | CC BY-SA 4.0 | Credit required; edited emoji must stay CC BY-SA | Medium | Avoid for pictures you will edit |
| IconScout, Blush, Icons8 | Large marketplaces of icons and illustrations | Licence pages blocked us (HTTP 403): unverified | Unverified | Possibly high: unverified | Read the licence before any use |
| Your own photos and commissioned art | Materials photographed in Bengaluru; 20–30 pieces of Indian clothing and props (thela, tricycle cart, platform scale, sacks, bales, tempo) | Written copyright transfer, plus signed consent from anyone photographed | None | **Highest** | Use for the material tiles and 5–10 main scenes |
risks: Licence terms change over time. unDraw's terms were revised in 2026, and Storyset requires credit 'as stated from time to time'. Record the date each licence was checked and re-check before launch.

unDraw and DrawKit forbid using their art to train or feed AI tools. Generating 'Indian versions' of their illustrations with AI would breach the licence, and copyright in AI-generated art is unclear.

Share-alike licences (OpenMoji, CC BY-SA files on Wikimedia) could require Luma.Green's edited pictures to be released under the same licence. Scattered CC BY icons build up credits that are easy to forget.
Pictures of kabadiwalas and waste workers can slide into stereotypes (dirt, poverty). Depict them as skilled professionals, as the name Saathi intends, and review the art with pilot users.
Synthetic voices may mispronounce trade words (raddi, bhangar) or local place names, or use the wrong dialect, which erodes trust. Speaking live details adds cost and delay.

Next's offline detection is experimental and Next says not to use it in production yet. Offline caching can leave users stuck on an old version of the app, and Background Sync works only in Chrome and Edge.
Bigger buttons and fewer words mean more screens. If the order of steps isn't thought through, users end up scrolling, which NN/g found hurts low-literacy readers.
Switching to international digits may annoy some Bengali or Marathi users who expect their own script's digits. Test it before rolling it out.
Shared phones: family members can see code SMSs and tracking links, so tracking pages must show little personal data.

The extra auto-fill line makes each code SMS longer. In Kannada or Hindi, where one SMS holds only 70 characters, that may mean two SMSs per code and higher cost. Adding the line after DLT approval means approving the templates again.
openQuestions: Which languages do the actual pilot kabadiwalas and households in Bengaluru read and speak, and how many can read numbers but not words? A 5-person check would settle it.
Do Bengali, Marathi and Urdu pilot users prefer international digits or their own script's digits for prices and weights?
Do users recognise materials faster from real photos or from drawn pictures? This needs a quick recognition test before the material tiles are fixed.
Do the bin colours in the new Solid Waste Management Rules (wet, dry, sanitary, special care) clash with the planned material colours? Not checked here.
Which text-to-speech service for the pilot: Google's Chirp 3 HD, the free Indic Parler-TTS, or Bhashini/Sarvam? Pricing and startup access to Bhashini were not checked.

Does the Convex client keep unsent changes after the app reloads offline, or does the weigh-and-pay queue need to be stored on the phone by us? Next's automatic retries cover its own form actions, not Convex updates.
What are the licence terms of IconScout, Blush and Icons8? Their pages blocked our access.
Which Indian accessibility rules (the RPwD Act 2016, the Indian standard IS 17802, the government's GIGW 3.0 guidelines) apply to a private platform like Luma.Green? Not checked here.
What budget and timeline are there for commissioning a custom set of Indian clothing and props for the illustrations?

result.headline: In Indian recycling, the money has followed regulation rather than households: Recykal's revenue went from ₹1.8 crore (FY19) to ₹21.2 crore (FY20) after it moved from a scrap marketplace to EPR compliance. The SWM Rules 2026 (in force since 1 April 2026) and the rise in required recycled content for rigid plastic packaging (30% in FY2025-26, 60% from FY2028-29) make Luma.Green's weighed hand-off records the thing to sell, not commissions on household pickups.

findings.point: Revenue in Indian recycling has followed compliance, not household pickups.
findings.detail: Recykal (Hyderabad) started in 2017 as a marketplace linking collection centres to recyclers. In 2019 it moved to EPR compliance services for brands. Forbes India reports revenue of ₹1.8 crore in FY19 (loss ₹3.6 crore), rising to ₹21.2 crore in FY20 (loss ₹5.3 crore). Its funding went: $2M pre-Series A (June 2019, Triton and Ajay Parekh); a Series A from Circulate Capital (Dec 2020); $22M in Jan 2022 with Morgan Stanley; and a reported ₹110 crore in April 2024. By 2023 it worked with 620+ brands, 675 recyclers and 12,000 businesses and had moved more than 1 million tonnes. The founder said each reverse-logistics order took 45 to 60 minutes. Lesson for Luma.Green: sell the compliance-grade record of the chain, and treat households as the source of supply.

findings.point: A household pickup is worth about ₹250. A commission on it cannot fund the company, and it pushes people to trade off the platform.
findings.detail: Scrapuncle's published rates for Delhi NCR and Bengaluru, per kg: newspaper and books ₹11–13, cardboard and plastic ₹7–8, iron ₹20–25, steel ₹34–42, aluminium ₹90–112, brass ₹260–325, copper ₹404–505. At mid-rates, a typical 20 kg basket of paper, cardboard, plastic and iron pays the household about ₹246 (our calculation). A 5% fee on that is about ₹12, far less than a 45 to 60 minute pickup costs. Bill Gurley's argument about platform fees applies: a high fee drives suppliers off the platform and invites competitors, and cash or UPI at the door makes going direct easy. Keep household and kabadiwala transactions free, and earn further up the chain, where lots are bigger and metals lift the value per tonne.

findings.point: The Solid Waste Management Rules 2026 create a new paying customer: bulk waste generators, including apartment societies.
findings.detail:
From CPCB's fee guidelines (September 2026): MoEFCC notified the SWM Rules 2026 on 27 Jan 2026. They replace the 2016 rules and took effect on 1 Apr 2026.
- **Who counts as a bulk generator:** any building of at least 20,000 m², or one using at least 40,000 litres of water a day, or one generating at least 100 kg of waste a day. This includes residential societies, offices, institutions, hotels, malls and markets.
- **What they must do:** register on a central CPCB portal, file annual returns by 30 June, and buy Extended Bulk Waste Generator Responsibility (EBWGR) certificates covering the waste they generate.
- **Sorters:** every entity that sorts dry waste into recyclable and non-recyclable must register with the local body (Rule 9(1)).
- **Portal fees:** one-time registration of ₹1,000–5,000 for residential societies and ₹2,000–10,000 for commercial generators, plus 25% of that every year. Sorting and processing sites (MRFs) pay ₹1,500–7,500.

Many mid-size and large apartment societies in Bengaluru are likely to qualify (our inference). That makes them a recurring, compliance-driven channel for pickups, weighed receipts and the data for their annual returns.

findings.point: Plastic EPR requires the recycled content of rigid packaging to rise from 30% to 60%, so brands need feedstock they can trace.
findings.detail:
Plastic Waste Management (Amendment) Rules 2022 (G.S.R. 133(E), 16 Feb 2022).
- **Required recycled content:** Category I rigid packaging needs 30% in FY2025-26, 40% in FY2026-27, 50% in FY2027-28 and 60% from FY2028-29. Category II goes from 10% to 20%; Category III from 5% to 10%.
- **Minimum recycling:** for Category I, 60% of the EPR target in FY2025-26, rising to 80% from FY2027-28.
- **Certificates:** only registered plastic waste processors may issue them. The volume cannot exceed the processor's installed capacity, each certificate must carry GST data, and a processor found giving false information is barred for one year.

Weighed, verified chain-of-custody records are what recyclers need to back their certificates. Check for later amendments before quoting these percentages to investors.

findings.point: Trading in EPR certificates is run by the government within a fixed price band, so Luma.Green should supply evidence rather than run a certificate exchange.
findings.detail:
The E-Waste (Management) Amendment Rules 2024 (G.S.R. 164(E), 8 Mar 2024) do three things:
- They let the Central Government set up platforms for exchanging EPR certificates by order.
- They require CPCB to set a maximum and minimum certificate price of 100% and 30% of the penalty for not meeting EPR obligations.
- They require registered entities to trade through the portal within that band.

The margin on trading certificates is therefore capped and the venue is fixed. The businesses Luma.Green can defend are evidence packs for registered recyclers and producer responsibility organisations (PROs), and help with registrations and annual returns.

findings.point: Carbon is possible upside, not part of the base case: none of India's offset methods covers dry recyclables yet.
findings.detail:
The Indian Carbon Market portal lists 12 approved offset methods:
- 3 energy
- 2 industrial
- 3 waste: landfill methane recovery, flaring or use of landfill gas, and compressed biogas
- 2 forestry
- 2 agriculture

It also has tools for composting and landfill emissions. None of these covers recycling paper, plastic or metal.

In the voluntary market, Verra's plastic program issues credits for collecting and for recycling plastic. One credit is one tonne, counted only above a baseline that is reviewed every 7 years, and projects must protect waste pickers. The program is still small: 40+ projects, 40,000+ credits, 25+ countries. For now, show CO2e avoided as an impact measure, and pursue plastic credits later through a registered project partner.

findings.point: Traceability is what unlocks trade finance, and Indian lending rules decide how a platform can earn from it.
findings.detail:
Metycle (European metals trading) traded more than $120M in 12 months, up 150% on the year, and secured a $150M credit facility from Rivonia Road Capital. Its TrustTrack record ties origin, composition, processing and delivery to each batch, for both buyers and lenders.

In India, RBI's Digital Lending guidelines (2 Sept 2022) set these rules for platforms that refer borrowers:
- The lender pays the referring platform's fees; the borrower does not.
- Loan money and repayments move directly between borrower and lender, never through a third party's pooled account.
- Borrowers get a key fact statement.
- Lenders publish the list of platforms they use.

So Luma.Green can earn referral fees paid by lenders, using its receipts as evidence for credit decisions, but it must never hold or route loan money.

findings.point: Bengaluru already has household-pickup competitors. Luma.Green's way in is to equip the existing kabadiwalas and connect them to yards, recyclers and manufacturers.
findings.detail: Scrapuncle serves Delhi NCR and Bengaluru with a published rate list. The Kabadiwala operates in 15 cities including Bangalore. It claims 100,000+ customers, 81.1 million kg kept out of landfill and 500+ corporate partners, sells plastic EPR services as a PRO, and says it raised about ₹3 crore. Scrapuncle sends its own trained crews and The Kabadiwala runs its own collection service, so neither works through the local kabadiwala. Luma.Green instead gives the city's existing kabadiwalas rate cards, weigh-and-record and stock tracking, and links them to yards, recyclers and manufacturers. Neither competitor connects the whole chain like this.

findings.point: India's waste gap is large and measurable: 21% of municipal waste is unaccounted for, and Bengaluru separates only about half its waste at source.
findings.detail:
CPCB's 2023-24 annual report gives these national figures, in tonnes per day:
- 1,85,195 generated
- 1,79,479 collected (about 97%)
- 1,13,935 processed or treated (62%)
- 32,531 landfilled (17%)
- 38,729 unaccounted (21%)

Karnataka generates 12,140 tonnes a day, treats 7,694 and landfills 3,048. It has 316 urban local bodies and 201 dumpsites. BBMP (Bengaluru) separates 53–55% of waste at source. The investor pitch: Luma.Green records the flows the formal system cannot see.

findings.point: Investors will judge this marketplace on how often buyers and sellers are matched, how fast, the fee it keeps, and two separate retention curves.
findings.detail:
a16z lists 13 marketplace measures:
- match rate and market depth
- time to match
- how concentrated the trade is
- the share of each transaction kept as revenue (take rate)
- unit economics
- how many users also use rivals, and the cost of switching
- user cohorts, retention of the core action and revenue retention
- retention in new versus established markets
- the spread of engagement among the heaviest users

Lenny Rachitsky's benchmarks for 6-month retention: consumer transactional products about 30% good and 50% great; small-business software about 60% and 80%. For 12-month net revenue retention in small-business software, about 90% is good and 110% great.

For Luma.Green, households follow the consumer curve and kabadiwalas and yards follow the small-business curve. Retention in each new cluster compared with the first proves the city playbook.

findings.point: The strongest lasting advantage available is a standard: open material codes and a receipt format that others adopt.
findings.detail:
NFX ranks standards-based ('protocol') network effects second of 16 types, after physical networks. Marketplace effects rank 6th and data effects 9th. Local marketplaces whose value levels off as they grow, which is what a household pickup market is, rank 8th.

ReMA's scrap specifications (July 2026 edition) show how a standard wins. They are free to use and cover ferrous and non-ferrous metals, paper, plastics, electronics, glass and tyres. Anyone can propose changes. Traders use them as the common language in contracts and agree any departures in writing.

India has recent examples of open protocols being adopted: the Beckn protocol runs ONDC, the Unified Energy Interface, the Unified Health Interface and Bengaluru's Namma Yatri.

findings.point: Saathi gig work in Karnataka will carry a welfare fee of 1–5% of each payout.
findings.detail:
PRS summarises the Karnataka Platform-based Gig Workers (Social Security and Welfare) Bill 2025. An ordinance came in May 2025 and the Bill was introduced on 12 Aug 2025.
- **Who it covers:** an aggregator is any digital intermediary that connects buyers and sellers of goods or services.
- **Fee:** the aggregator pays a welfare fee of 1–5% of each payout to a gig worker, with the rate set by category.
- **Duties:** register with the Welfare Board within 45 days of the law starting, share worker data and report every payment.

Any Saathi job priced on Luma.Green must include this fee and keep a ledger of payouts.

findings.point: Rooftop solar leads are a cheap extra sale to households the kabadiwala has already met at the door.
findings.detail: PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana was approved in Feb 2024. It has ₹75,021 crore to put rooftop solar on 1 crore homes, with subsidies of up to ₹78,000 per household depending on consumption. These figures come from a Wikipedia summary; confirm them on pmsuryaghar.gov.in. Households who have just had a paid pickup, and the roofs of yards, are natural leads for approved solar vendors. We don't know what vendors pay per lead, so treat this as small upside.

findings.point: CPCB's state figures, together with the languages Luma.Green already supports, give the order for expanding city by city.
findings.detail:
Municipal waste generated per day by state (CPCB 2023-24), with the unaccounted share where large:
- Maharashtra: 24,299 tonnes
- Uttar Pradesh: 20,114 tonnes
- Tamil Nadu: 17,843 tonnes (8,630 unaccounted)
- West Bengal: 14,072 tonnes (9,585 unaccounted)
- Karnataka: 12,140 tonnes
- Gujarat: 12,000 tonnes
- Telangana: 11,714 tonnes
- Delhi: 11,342 tonnes (3,464 unaccounted)

The main language of every one of these states is already among Luma.Green's 12 languages. Each new city should be set up by changing data, not code: floor and fallback price tables, local material names, pollution-board document types and local-body registration.

recommendations.feature: Traction dashboard: extend the admin pilot-numbers page into a view for investors
recommendations.why: a16z's marketplace measures (match rate, time to match, take rate, retention by cohort and by city) are what seed investors ask for, and the events table from ADR 0012 already captures most of them. Show kg traced by material, recorded rupee value of trades, completion rate, median time to accept, how close the AI's weight estimate is to the weighed kg, repeat households, active verified businesses, 'shadow revenue' (what fees would have earned if switched on) and CO2e avoided. Label the prototype clearly as demo data.

recommendations.feature: Trace view: one short code or QR per lot, linking household receipts to kabadiwala stock, the yard lot and the recycler batch
recommendations.why: It shows the core idea, recording every hand-off, on one screen. Plastic EPR certificates must match real capacity and carry GST data, and the SWM Rules 2026 require registrations and annual returns. Metycle's batch-level record backs a $150M credit facility. Export the chain as CSV or JSON with GST number, material code, weight and date so it can feed CPCB returns.

recommendations.feature: Open material codes v0.1: an admin-editable table, a public page and a CSV/JSON download under the CC BY 4.0 licence
recommendations.why: Standards-based network effects are the strongest kind (NFX ranks them 2nd of 16), and ReMA's specifications show that a free list of grades that anyone can propose changes to becomes the trade's common language. Each code carries names in 12 languages, a photo, a unit, the matching ReMA grade, the HSN tax code and the CPCB category. Because it is a table, it can be changed without code.

recommendations.feature: Pricing plans stored as data, with 'shadow revenue'
recommendations.why: Keep every fee at ₹0 during the pilot: Gurley's point is that low fees win, and cash at the door makes high fees leak. But store plans per city and per stream (pickup fee, kabadiwala Pro, yard workspace, fee on business-to-business lots, society plan) and calculate what each would have earned. Investors see the model, users see no friction, and switching a fee on is a data change.

recommendations.feature: Trust norms: a public 'Luma Verified' badge plus a weighing standard in weigh-and-record
recommendations.why: Verification is already done by hand. Show the checks passed (ID and selfie, pollution-board consent PDF, GST if given, date verified) as a badge that can be withdrawn. For each weighing, require a photo of the scale, confirmation from both sides and a way to flag a dispute. This turns the pilot's 'estimated vs weighed kg' measure into evidence, and it is the start of a certification others can refer to.

recommendations.feature: Accounts for apartment societies and other bulk generators under the SWM Rules 2026
recommendations.why: Since 1 Apr 2026, anyone generating 100 kg or more of waste a day, including residential societies, must register on CPCB's portal, file returns by 30 June and buy EBWGR certificates. A society account would give scheduled dry-waste pickups by a verified kabadiwala, monthly weighed statements and a yearly summary for the return. That is recurring revenue driven by compliance (our guess: ₹500–2,000 a month) and it brings many households at once. Start with 3–5 Bengaluru societies as design partners.

recommendations.feature: Yard workspace: a light software product for yards
recommendations.why: Yards need purchase receipts, a stock ledger, sale lots, GST invoice fields and a record of their Rule 9(1) registration with the local body. Small-business software keeps 60–80% of users after 6 months, which makes this the most predictable revenue. Free in the pilot; our guess is ₹1,500–5,000 a month later.

recommendations.feature: Bengaluru price index: weekly median prices per material from receipts and yards' buying prices, shown next to the admin floor price
recommendations.why: Households already compare published rates (Scrapuncle lists ₹11–13/kg for newspaper and ₹7–8/kg for plastic). A neutral index built from real weighed receipts becomes a reference price and a public search-friendly page. It improves as more trades are recorded, and later it can be a paid data feed or report for recyclers and manufacturers.

recommendations.feature: Saathi payout ledger that includes Karnataka's welfare fee
recommendations.why: Karnataka's gig-worker law sets a welfare fee of 1–5% on each payout, requires aggregators to register within 45 days and to report payments. Record every Saathi payout and its fee from the first day, and keep paid Saathi jobs switched off until the fee rate for Luma.Green's category is known.

recommendations.feature: Evidence packs for registered recyclers and PROs, covering EPR and recycled content
recommendations.why: Rigid packaging must contain 30% recycled plastic in FY2025-26 and 60% from FY2028-29. EPR certificates trade only on government platforms, at 30–100% of the non-compliance penalty. So sell verified chain-of-custody evidence priced per tonne, and never trade certificates. Add plastic-credit projects later through a partner registered with Verra.

recommendations.feature: Working-capital loan referrals to an RBI-regulated lender, based on platform receipts
recommendations.why: Kabadiwalas pay households in cash, and yards wait to be paid by recyclers, so both need working capital. Their receipts are evidence a lender can use. Under RBI's digital lending rules the lender pays the referral fee and money moves only between lender and borrower, so Luma.Green earns without holding any funds.

recommendations.feature: Rooftop solar leads under PM Surya Ghar, for households and yards
recommendations.why: The scheme has ₹75,021 crore for 1 crore homes, with subsidies up to ₹78,000, and households already trust the app after a paid pickup. Pass leads to approved vendors for a fee per installation. This is a low-effort add-on, not core business.

result.artifactMarkdown:
# Luma.Green: investor narrative (one-page outline)

_Draft for the investor prototype, 29 Sep 2026. Figures marked (H) are our guesses, to be tested in the pilot. Every other figure comes from a source in the research notes._

**In one line.** Luma.Green records India's informal recycling chain. Every hand-off from household to manufacturer is weighed, priced and traceable, in 12 languages, on a basic smartphone.

## 1. Problem
- India generates **1,85,195 tonnes a day** of municipal waste. **38,729 tonnes a day (21%)** is neither processed nor landfilled; nobody can say where it went (CPCB 2023-24).
- Karnataka generates **12,140 tonnes a day**. Bengaluru separates only **53–55%** at source.
- Recyclables do move, through kabadiwalas and yards, but on cash, guessed weights and phone calls. There are no published prices, no records and no proof of origin.

## 2. Why now
- **SWM Rules 2026, in force since 1 Apr 2026.** Anyone generating 100 kg or more a day, including residential societies, must register on a CPCB portal, file returns by 30 June and buy certificates for the waste they generate (EBWGR certificates). Every dry-waste sorter must register with the local body.
- **Plastic EPR.** Rigid packaging must contain **30% recycled plastic in FY2025-26, rising to 60% from FY2028-29**. Certificates must match a recycler's real capacity and carry GST data.
- **Regulated certificate markets.** E-waste EPR certificates trade on a government portal at **30–100%** of the penalty for non-compliance. What is scarce is proof, not certificates.
- UPI payments, cheap photo-recognition AI and first-time smartphone users make a three-tap household flow possible.

## 3. Product (working prototype)
- **Household:** photo, then AI estimate, then pickup, then paid in cash or UPI.
- **Kabadiwala:** booking requests, their own rate card above an admin floor price, weigh-and-record, stock.
- **Yard, recycler, manufacturer:** lots to buy and sell, and a trace view.
- **Saathi:** short paid jobs.
- **Admin:** every business checked by hand.

## 4. Business model: free at the door, paid further up the chain
| Stage | Revenue stream | Who pays | Price (H) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Pilot (Oct–Dec 2026) | Nothing charged; "shadow revenue" (what fees would have earned) is measured | — | — |
| After the pilot | Compliance plan for apartment societies and other bulk generators | Societies, offices | ₹500–2,000 a month |
| After the pilot | Yard workspace: stock, receipts, GST fields, SWM records | Yards | ₹1,500–5,000 a month |
| Scale | Fee on business-to-business lots (kabadiwala to yard to recycler to manufacturer) | Buyer | 0.5–2% of lot value |
| Scale | Evidence packs for EPR and recycled content | Recyclers, PROs, brands | ₹ per tonne |
| Scale | Price index and data feed | Recyclers, manufacturers | Subscription |
| Scale | Referrals for working-capital loans and rooftop solar | Regulated lenders, solar vendors | Per loan or per installation |
| Upside | Share of plastic-credit revenue through a registered partner | Credit buyers | % of each credit |

- **Why no commission from households.** A 20 kg basket pays the household about ₹250 at Bengaluru rates. A 5% fee is about ₹12, less than the cost of a pickup that takes 45–60 minutes, and cash at the door makes it easy to skip the app.
- **Example of a mature city (H).** 500 societies at ₹1,000 plus 50 yards at ₹3,000 plus 1% of 3,000 tonnes a month at ₹25/kg comes to about **₹14 lakh a month (about ₹1.7 crore a year)**, before EPR, data and referral income.

## 5. Why we win
- **Equip kabadiwalas, don't replace them.** Competitors in Bengaluru run their own pickup service. We give the city's existing kabadiwalas the tools and connect them to buyers further up the chain.
- **Three effects that build on each other.** Busy local clusters come first. Every weighed receipt then sharpens the AI estimates and the price index. Finally, open material codes and a receipt format that others adopt make us the standard; ReMA's scrap specifications are the global example.
- **Trust as a rule of the platform.** Participants are verified, weighing follows a set standard and the record of each lot is unbroken. Regulators, brands and lenders can accept that as evidence.

## 6. Comparable companies
| Company | Model | Numbers | Lesson |
|---|---|---|---|
| Recykal, Hyderabad | Marketplace (2017), then EPR compliance (2019) | Revenue ₹1.8 crore FY19, ₹21.2 crore FY20; $22M in 2022 with Morgan Stanley; ₹110 crore in 2024 (reported); 620+ brands, 675 recyclers | Revenue follows compliance |
| Metycle, Europe | Metals trading with records for every batch | $120M traded in 12 months (+150%); $150M credit facility | Traceability unlocks loans |
| The Kabadiwala, Bhopal | Own pickup service plus plastic EPR services | 15 cities including Bengaluru; 100,000+ customers; 81.1 million kg; about ₹3 crore raised | Household-first businesses stay small |
| Scrapuncle, Delhi | Own pickup crews, published rate list | Delhi NCR and Bengaluru | Direct competitor in the pilot city |

## 7. KPIs to show
| KPI | Definition | Prototype | Pilot, by Dec 2026 (H) | Ready for seed round (H) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Kg traced | Weighed kg per month, by material | Demo data | 5 tonnes in total | 100+ tonnes a month |
| Recorded value | ₹ on weighed receipts | Demo | ₹75,000+ in total | ₹20 lakh+ a month |
| Completion | Pickups weighed ÷ pickups booked | Demo | 80% or more | 85% or more |
| Time to accept | Median minutes from booking to acceptance | Demo | 15 min or less | 10 min or less |
| Estimate accuracy | Median gap between the AI's kg estimate and the weighed kg | Demo | Within 30% | Within 20% |
| Household repeat | Share of households booking again within 6 months | — | Track | 30% or more (50% is great) |
| Business retention | Kabadiwalas and yards still active after 6 months | — | Track | 60% or more (80% is great) |
| Receipt coverage | Completed pickups with a weighed receipt | Demo | 100% | 100% |
| Business-to-business match rate | Share of kabadiwala stock posts collected within 7 days | Demo | First trades | 60% or more |
| Cluster retention | Retention in the newest cluster compared with the first | — | — | Newer at least equal to older |
| Verification time | Hours from application to decision | Live | 24 h or less | 24 h or less |
| Shadow revenue and fee share | What each stream would earn if its fee were on | Demo | Track | Paying customers in 2 streams |
| Impact | Tonnes diverted; CO2e avoided (method published, not sold as credits) | Demo | Track | Method checked by a third party |

Retention bars come from public benchmarks for 6-month retention: 30% good and 50% great for consumer transaction apps; 60% good and 80% great for small-business software.

## 8. How we expand
- **The unit is a cluster:** 1 yard, 15–30 kabadiwalas within about 3 km, 2,000–5,000 households and 3–5 societies. A city is 5–10 clusters.
- **A new city is data, not code:** floor and fallback price tables, local material names, pollution-board document types, local-body registration, one operations lead, one anchor recycler and one waste-picker organisation as a partner.
- **Order**, based on CPCB tonnage and the languages already built:
  1. Bengaluru
  2. Mysuru and Hubballi (same language and pollution board)
  3. Hyderabad, Chennai and Pune/Mumbai (state totals of 11,714, 17,843 and 24,299 tonnes a day)
  4. Kolkata, Ahmedabad and Delhi NCR

## 9. Making our rules the industry's rules
- **Luma Material Codes and the hand-off receipt format**, published under the CC BY 4.0 licence. Each code has names in 12 languages, photos, and its matching ReMA grade, HSN tax code and CPCB category.
- **Open to change:** anyone can propose changes and every version is numbered.
- **Advisory group:** kabadiwalas, yards, recyclers and a waste-picker organisation. Once others use the codes, hand them to a neutral body to look after.
- **Weighing standard:** a government-stamped scale, a photo of the reading and confirmation from both sides.
- **Luma Verified badge:** shown on checked businesses and withdrawn if they break the rules.

## 10. Risks and how we handle them
- **Trading off the platform:** no commission on household pickups.
- **Regulated certificate markets:** we sell evidence, never certificates.
- **Carbon:** reported as an impact measure only, until an approved method covers recycling.
- **Karnataka gig-worker law:** the 1–5% welfare fee is built into Saathi pricing.
- **Lending rules:** referral fees paid by the lender, and we never hold loan money.
- **Demo data:** always labelled as demo.

**Ask:** ₹___ for ___ months to reach the seed-round column above in Bengaluru.
risks: Trading off the platform: after one booking through the app, a household and kabadiwala can deal directly in cash, and any per-pickup fee speeds this up (Gurley).
Weak household unit economics: about ₹250 per 20 kg pickup, and 45–60 minutes of reverse logistics per order (Recykal). Pickups alone will never pay for the company.

Regulated certificate markets: EPR certificates are exchanged on government platforms at 30–100% of the non-compliance penalty, and processors who give false data are barred for a year. A partner's fraud would taint Luma.Green's records.

Carbon expectations: no Indian offset method covers dry recyclables, and voluntary plastic credits are small (40,000+ credits worldwide). Do not put carbon revenue in the base-case model shown to investors.
Gig-worker law: Karnataka's 1–5% welfare fee, registration within 45 days and duty to share data may apply to Saathi jobs.
Loan referrals need a regulated lending partner and strict compliance with RBI rules: the lender pays the fee, and no loan money passes through Luma.Green.
Competition in Bengaluru from companies that run their own pickup service (Scrapuncle, The Kabadiwala) and from EPR service providers.
Investor demo risk: the prototype runs on demo data, and unlabelled numbers could be read as real traction.
Changing rules: the plastic EPR rules have been amended several times since 2022, so re-check the recycled-content percentages before putting them in a deck.
Adoption of the standard: if the material codes look proprietary or change unpredictably, competitors and regulators will not adopt them.
openQuestions: Under the SWM Rules 2026, who issues EBWGR certificates and at what price? Can a network of kabadiwalas and yards supply them to Bengaluru societies? (We need the text of the 27 Jan 2026 notification.)
What are kabadiwalas' real gross margins per material, and will they pay a monthly subscription or only per lead?
What are typical kabadiwala-to-yard lot sizes, how many days of credit are given, and who transports the material? This sizes both the business-to-business fee and the need for financing.
Has Karnataka's gig-worker Bill been passed and brought into force, and what fee rate would apply to Saathi jobs?
Will Luma.Green count as an e-commerce operator under GST (and so have to collect tax at source) once trades or escrow go live?
Do CPCB's EPR and SWM portals accept bulk uploads or API connections from outside record systems?
Which neutral body should look after the material codes in the long run: an industry association, a BIS committee, or a foundation?
What are the current recycled-content requirements after any 2024–2026 amendments to the plastic rules?

result.lead: Luma.Green becomes the record-keeping and trading layer for India's informal recycling chain. Every hand-off from household to manufacturer is weighed, priced, verified and traceable, in 12 languages on a basic Android phone, and the platform earns further up the chain rather than at the doorstep. The first thing it proves, in Bengaluru, is that one bale at a recycler can be traced back to the individual household pickups it came from. Each link carries a confirmed weight, a verified buyer and a receipt that both sides agreed to, which is the missing evidence behind about 7 lakh fake EPR certificates and ₹2,384 crore of scrap invoices for goods that never moved.

Exchange: stock board, pooled collection, orders
Impact: EPR evidence, carbon estimates, solar

Cash or P2P UPI for weighed kg
