personas.who: A resident of a Bengaluru flat who sells newspaper, cartons, PET and metal a few times a year; often a woman managing the home.
personas.needs: A fair, visible price before booking, a pickup that actually turns up, honest weighing, and cash or UPI before the kabadiwala leaves.
personas.device: Own Android phone, Chrome; sometimes a shared family phone
personas.language: Kannada, Tamil, Telugu, Urdu, Hindi or English; mostly literate
personas.companyServes: No account. Photo, then AI estimate, then side-by-side nearby shops with their rates, then booking with an SMS code, a tracking link, a receipt confirmed with a handover code, and recycle points.

personas.who: An older or less-schooled householder in a peri-urban area with bulky metal, appliances and raddi.
personas.needs: No typing, pictures and voice, and help from a person.
personas.language: Kannada, Tamil, Telugu or Urdu; limited reading
personas.companyServes: A Hear-it button on each step, one-tap call and WhatsApp, and a kabadiwala or Saathi who books on their behalf (the household confirms by SMS code).

personas.who: Committee or facility manager of a society, office, hotel or campus producing 100 kg or more of waste a day.
personas.needs: Registration and annual returns under the SWM Rules 2026, verified vendors only, and monthly kg figures by waste stream.
personas.companyServes: Scheduled pickups by a verified kabadiwala, monthly weighed statements and a yearly summary for the CPCB return (pilot design partners, paid plan later).

personas.who: Owner of a small scrap shop handling about 250–300 kg a day, often unregistered for GST, sometimes with a cycle cart or auto.
personas.needs: More households, stable prices, no weight disputes, buyers for sorted stock, and screens that need little reading.
personas.language: Kannada, Tamil, Telugu, Urdu, Hindi or Bengali; many with little formal schooling
personas.companyServes: Requests with auto-accept, today's route, weigh-and-pay in half-kilo steps, their own rate card above the floor, stock and sorting, and posting stock to yards. Free.

personas.who: A waste picker or someone looking for quick gig work: pickups, sorting shifts, cleaning. Often a migrant whose documents have lapsed.
personas.needs: Pay shown before accepting, safe work, IDs accepted other than Aadhaar, and a fair appeal if their account is paused.
personas.language: Kannada, Tamil, Telugu or Bengali; low literacy
personas.companyServes: Onboarding with a driving licence, voter ID, BBMP card or NGO letter plus a selfie, a Saathi Ready picture module, job cards with hazards and PPE, and a work record usable for NAMASTE and e-Shram. Pay stays off-platform.

personas.who: Runs a ward dry-waste collection centre with 20–25 workers, often supported by Hasiru Dala; its agreement with the city has lapsed.
personas.needs: Buyers, a sale register the city will accept, and evidence for renewing its agreement and claiming NAMASTE fees.
personas.companyServes: A yard account with a DWCC flag: daily weight sheet, sale register and monthly report, plus access to recyclers.

personas.who: Buys 1–30 t a day from kabadiwalas, sorts and bales, and sells to recyclers. Pays cash now and gets paid late.
personas.needs: Supply nearby, full trucks, weight and quality it can trust, and GST paperwork on metal (reverse charge, 2% TDS).
personas.language: Local language plus English for documents
personas.companyServes: Stock map, pooled collection, weight slips from both sides, grade cards, trade document pack, tax flags, Tally export, and a solar savings card.

personas.who: Staff member at a yard or recycler gate who weighs trucks in and out.
personas.needs: Three taps per truck, in their own language.
personas.companyServes: A gate screen: vehicle number, gross, tare and net weight, a slip photo, and an automatic flag when the gap is over 1%.

personas.who: A registered plastic, paper or metal recycler with a KSPCB consent and CPCB processor registration.
personas.needs: Graded feedstock, proof of post-consumer origin for EPR, production kept within capacity, and a clean audit trail.
personas.companyServes: Verified supply, lot passports, the EPR purchase register in CPCB field order, capacity warnings and a compliance vault.

personas.who: The accountant who runs Tally and files GST.
personas.needs: Vouchers without retyping, the e-way bill, reverse-charge and TDS flags, and 45-day MSME due dates.
personas.companyServes: Excel files in Tally's import layout, invoice fields, a payables and receivables clock, and UTR capture.

personas.who: A paper mill, steel furnace or packaging converter buying recycled input.
personas.needs: Steady, graded, tax-compliant domestic feedstock, and recycled-content proof for its customers.
personas.companyServes: Recycler output listings, orders, trace to origin, and simulated escrow now with real escrow later.

personas.who: An EPR compliance manager or verifier who has to meet recycled-content targets of 40% in 2026-27 for rigid packaging.
personas.needs: Believable evidence behind certificates after the fake-certificate scandals.
personas.companyServes: A read-only login with evidence packs per lot. Luma.Green never issues or trades certificates.

personas.who: Nodal officer at one of the Greater Bengaluru Authority corporations or at BSWML.
personas.needs: Ward-level dry-waste recovery figures and digital sale registers, which count towards Swachh Survekshan and GFC marks.
personas.companyServes: A read-only ward dashboard of totals, and a monthly export shaped for Swachhatam.

personas.who: A seed investor judging traction, or an NBFC judging a yard's creditworthiness.
personas.needs: Real flows, unit economics, retention, and verified trade history.
personas.companyServes: Traction dashboard with shadow revenue (investor), and a trade-history export shared with the user's consent (lender, later).

personas.who: The founder, and later an operations team, verifying every business by hand and handling support.
personas.needs: Verify within 12–24 h, change prices and rules without a code release, and settle disputes quickly.
personas.companyServes: Verification queue with checklists, price console, rulebook tables, complaints with timers, and an audit log.

sections.market:
Luma.Green sits on at least **₹1.8–2.1 lakh crore a year** of recyclable material, and households see only a fraction of its value. Ferrous scrap alone is 41 Mt at ₹36.5–41.5/kg ([BigMint](https://www.bigmint.co/insights/detail/india-bigmints-ferrous-scrap-index-slips-further-on-cautious-steel-market-sentiment-792405), [Dialogue Earth](https://www.eco-business.com/news/india-needs-more-scrap-to-boost-green-steelmaking-can-it-find-it/)). Paper adds about 17 Mt of recovered fibre ([W&R Mag](https://www.wasterecyclingmag.com/news/india-s-recovered-fibre-sector-requires-reforms-to-reach-full-potential)).

| Material (Bengaluru, Sep 2026) | Household gets, ₹/kg | Factory pays, ₹/kg | Household share |
|---|---|---|---|
| Copper | 500–588 | 1,394 MCX; 1,454 armature | 35–42% |
| Brass | 400–439 | 950–990 | 40–46% |
| Aluminium | 150–154 | 293–365 | about 50% |
| Aluminium cans | 60 | MCX aluminium 347.50 | about 17% |
| PET | 10 | 44 | about 23% |
| Cardboard | 3–8 | OCC 14–18 at mill | 20–55% |
| Iron | 22–39 | 36.5–41.5 | 55–100% |

Sources: [The Kabadiwala](https://www.thekabadiwala.com/scrap-rates/Bangalore), [scraprates](https://scraprates.in/bangalore), [MCX via Upstox](https://upstox.com/commodity-market-trading/mcx-copper-price/), [Shree Metal](https://shreemetalprices.com/delhi-scrap-prices-today/), [ScrapC](https://scrapc.com/news/pet-bottle-price/), [BIN](https://joinbin.com/scrap-rate-cardboard-india), [Aluminium Magazine](https://aluminiummagazine.com/mag/business/current-aluminium-price.html).

**What shapes the plan**
- The first mile is informal. 1.5–4 million waste pickers move 60–70% of urban recyclables ([DTE](https://www.downtoearth.org.in/waste/indias-waste-economy-runs-on-invisible-workers-climate-policy-keeps-forgetting-them)), and 80–85% of Bengaluru's dry waste passes through informal hands ([BBMP study](https://apps.bbmpgov.in/SWM/Home/Documents/ReportsandStudies/Extracting%20Value%20from%20Bengaluru's%20Dry%20Waste%20Chain_Full%20Report%20(Nov%202014).pdf)). Design for cash, first smartphones and GST as optional.
- Hand-offs run to 4–6 tiers. Model yards as one role with a size and tier attribute that can buy from other yards, instead of adding a role for every tier.
- Trust is weak at the scale. Bengaluru scrap shops were caught with remote-controlled chips in their scales ([Deccan Herald](https://www.deccanherald.com/india/karnataka/bengaluru/weighing-scale-racket-in-bengaluru-busted-by-kamakshipalya-police-1201713.html)), and Bengaluru Urban had 5,375 Legal Metrology cases in 17 months ([NewsKarnataka](https://newskarnataka.com/karnataka/bengaluru/fraud-in-weights-and-measurements-continues-despite-digital-advances-in-bengaluru/06112024)).
- Quality leaks value. Wet cardboard loses 30–50% ([BIN](https://joinbin.com/scrap-rate-cardboard-india)), so every B2B hand-off records gross, deduction, reason and net weight.
- India is short of domestic scrap. It imports about 7 Mt of recovered paper a year and a quarter of its ferrous scrap, so mills will pay for supply that is sorted and traceable.
- Bengaluru specifics: 119 of 198 DWCCs are still operating and their city agreements have lapsed ([Citizen Matters](https://citizenmatters.in/invisible-workers-visible-waste-bengalurus-waste-pickers-struggle-without-recognition/)). Mother tongues are Kannada 42%, Tamil 16%, Telugu 14% and Urdu 13% ([Census 2011](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bengaluru)).
- National figures conflict (e-waste is 1.4 Mt per CPCB against 6.19 Mt per NITI Aayog). Every investor number cites its source and definition. The ₹1.8–2.1 lakh crore figure is our own bottom-up estimate.
sections.competitors:
No competitor connects household bookings, kabadiwala tools and yard-to-factory trade on one platform. **Decision: equip the kabadiwalas who already exist, don't run a fleet, and lead the pitch with the traced chain.**

| Player | What they do | Scale | What we take from them |
|---|---|---|---|
| The Kabadiwala + Scrapr | Own fleet in small cities; a partner-kabadiwala marketplace in 25+ Bengaluru areas | 5,000+ kabadiwalas, $3.33M raised ([Sankalp](https://www.sankalpforum.com/from-college-frustration-to-organizing-indias-waste-economy-sankalpchangemakers-features-anurag-asati-co-founder-the-kabadiwala/), [Tracxn](https://tracxn.com/d/companies/the-kabadiwala/__m3UNbioxN9Vlb-olXsWxlH2fS3RjMA9DD-dTecfCnLc)) | Its top complaints are no-shows and requests that get stuck ([App Store](https://apps.apple.com/in/app/the-kabadiwala/id1610864605)). Reliability becomes our feature |
| ScrapUncle | Own crews, published rate cards | ₹22 Cr raised Jan 2026 ([Inc42](https://inc42.com/buzz/cleantech-startup-scrapuncle-raises-inr-22-cr-to-expand-presence-across-delhi-ncr/)) | Shows households prices before pickup and pays before leaving |
| Recykal (Uzed closed) | Household app lost money at 45–60 min per order; moved to B2B and EPR | ₹1,498 Cr gross revenue FY26 ([CSR Universe](https://thecsruniverse.com/articles/recykal-raises-usd-23-million-to-expand-circular-economy-technology-and-global-operations), [Forbes India](https://www.forbesindia.com/article/take-one-big-story-of-the-day/how-recykal-is-cleaning-up-the-mess/70177/1)) | Its document pack is now the norm; it deals only with GST-verified businesses, which leaves kabadiwalas to us |
| Attero MetalMandi | AI photo pricing for metal dealers | 15,000 t/month, not in Bengaluru ([Tribune](https://www.tribuneindia.com/news/business/atteros-metalmandi-crosses-2-lakh-downloads-targets-5x-growth-in-five-years/amp)) | Route material to recyclers' own buying apps rather than fight them |
| Hasiru Dala / HDI | DWCCs, fair-trade traceable plastic, bulk generators | 370+ bulk clients ([HDI](https://hasirudalainnovations.com/)) | Partner, don't compete: their DWCCs become our first yards and Saathi pool |
| Karo Sambhav, ReCircle, Banyan | PRO traceability, largely manual | 5,000 aggregators; 3,500 waste pickers | We produce the same proof automatically as part of daily work |
| Metaloop, Rubicon | Financed trades themselves; thin broker margins | Metaloop in restructuring since Jun 2026 ([Leadersnet](https://www.leadersnet.at/news/101092,bekanntes-austro-startup-schlittert-in-millionenpleite.html)) | Never pre-pay for trades, hold stock or hold anyone's money |

Differentiators to show investors, in order:
1. The lot passport from recycler back to household.
2. The photo estimate priced from our own tables.
3. A Kannada-first app built for low literacy, with voice.
4. Shop rates shown side by side, above an admin floor.
5. A free yard book that small yards will actually use.
sections.pricing:
**Material prices: build the board only from Luma.Green's own data.** No exchange feed is shown publicly. Money is stored in integer paise and weight in grams, and every table carries an effective date (ADR 0008).

| Layer | Decision | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Floors and fallbacks | Admin-edited per city and material. Suggested fallback = 28-day median; floor = 75% of fallback, rounded down to ₹0.50. Changes over 10% a week need a written reason. A suspend switch per material | Paper collection halved in the 2023 crash ([P&P Times](https://thepulpandpapertimes.com/news/price-of-waste-paper-plummeted-to-its-lowest-level-in-the-previous-five-months-881)) |
| Plausible bands | Min and max per material; the largest daily move allowed is ±10% for paper and plastic, ±5% for metals | Catches mistakes such as a stray ₹25/kg newspaper rate |
| Reference prices | Entered weekly by the admin with source and date; visible only to the admin and investor views | MCX allows delayed data only under an agreement; LME needs a US$25k/yr licence ([MCX](https://www.mcxindia.com/technology/datafeed), [LME](https://www.lme.com/en/market-data/market-data-licensing/data-distribution)) |
| Public board | /prices/bengaluru: range, typical price, 7-day change, Live or Guide, number of shops. Live needs 3 or more independent businesses and at least 1 trade. Sample-data badge in the prototype | Nobody publishes dated Bengaluru household prices |
| Freshness | Rate cards stay fresh for 14 days (paper, plastic) or 7 days (metals), with an SMS reminder; stale cards drop off the board | Paper fell 20% in 10 days in Feb 2024 ([P&P Times](https://thepulpandpapertimes.com/news/india/domestic-waste-paper-prices-1003)) |
| Honour rate | Compare each shop's posted rate with what its receipts actually paid; a gap flags the shop | Stops shops advertising a high rate to win bookings |

**Luma.Green's own revenue: free at the door, paid further up the chain.** A 20 kg basket pays the household about ₹250, so a 5% fee is about ₹12, less than the pickup costs, and cash makes skipping the app easy ([Gurley](https://abovethecrowd.com/2013/04/18/a-rake-too-far-optimal-platformpricing-strategy/)). The revenue streams live in a plans table, are all ₹0 in the pilot, and the dashboard shows the shadow revenue they would have earned.

| Stream | Payer | Price (hypothesis) | Starts |
|---|---|---|---|
| Society / bulk-generator compliance plan | RWAs, offices | ₹500–2,000/month | After the pilot |
| Yard workspace (book, documents, exports) | Yards, DWCCs | ₹1,500–5,000/month | After the pilot |
| B2B trade fee (plus escrow later) | Buyer | 0.5–1% of lot value | Scale |
| EPR evidence packs | Recyclers, PROs, brands | ₹ per tonne | Scale |
| Price index and data | Recyclers, manufacturers | Subscription | Scale |
| Loan and solar referrals | Lenders, installers | Per loan or install; the lender pays, never the borrower ([RBI](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/NotificationUser.aspx?Id=12848&Mode=0)) | Scale |
sections.compliance:
**The pilot stays out of the heavy regimes by keeping money off the platform. Every legal number lives in an admin-edited, dated Rulebook table, because at least six of them changed between Jul 2024 and Jan 2027.**

| Rule | Trigger / number | What Luma.Green does | When |
|---|---|---|---|
| RBI payment aggregators | Holding trade money needs an authorised PA; splitting payments to sellers needs ₹40 lakh of own turnover ([RBI MD](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/NotificationUser.aspx?Id=12896&Mode=0), [Route](https://razorpay.com/docs/payments/route/)) | Record payments only; escrow simulated in the prototype | Now |
| GST e-commerce TCS | 0.5%, only once Luma collects the money (s.52) | An 'ECO switch' that turns on TCS and GSTR-8 when escrow starts | Scale |
| Income-tax e-commerce TDS | 0.1%, and may apply even to direct payments (s.393) | Get a CA opinion before B2B trades; capture PAN optionally | Pilot |
| Metal scrap GST | Reverse charge from unregistered sellers; self-invoice within 30 days; 2% TDS above ₹2.5 lakh ([06/2024](https://gstcouncil.gov.in/sites/default/files/2024-10/ctr-06-2024.pdf), [25/2024](https://gstcouncil.gov.in/sites/default/files/2024-10/ct-25-2024.pdf)) | Flags and self-invoice data on each trade | Pilot |
| E-way bill | Over ₹50,000 by motor vehicle in Karnataka; handcarts exempt ([Rule 138](https://taxinformation.cbic.gov.in/content/html/tax_repository/gst/rules/cgst_rules/active/chapter16/rule138_v1.00.html)) | Yes/no checker plus pre-filled Part A | Pilot |
| SWM Rules 2026 | In force 1 Apr 2026; bulk generators and dry-waste sorters register and file returns; trade only with registered parties ([SWM 2026](https://cpcb.gov.in/uploads/MSW/SWM_2026.pdf)) | Registration fields on every org; optional 'registered sellers only' filter; returns export | Pilot |
| Legal Metrology | Electronic scales re-verified every 12 months; under-weighing is an offence ([r.27](https://indiankanoon.org/doc/67045693/), [e-Mapan](https://emapan.karnataka.gov.in/)) | Scale register, verified-scale badge, scale photo per weighing | Now |
| E-Commerce Amendment Rules 2026 | From 1 Jan 2027: grievance acknowledged in 48 h and resolved in 1 month, seller disclosure, ranking explanation, yearly dark-pattern audit ([G.S.R. 789(E)](https://consumeraffairs.gov.in/public/upload/admin/cmsfiles/whatsnews/E_Commerce_Amendment_Rules_2026_2026-09-11_18-12-39.pdf)) | Grievance desk, legal-pages pack | Pilot |
| IT Rules 2021 | Grievance acknowledged in 24 h and resolved in 15 days; 36 h takedowns | Same desk; admin takedown action with audit log | Pilot |
| DPDP Rules 2025 | Core duties from about 13 May 2027; breach reported within 72 h; penalties up to ₹250 cr ([DPDP](https://www.dpdpa.com/DPDP_Rules_2025_English_only.pdf)) | Notices per role, consent log, household photos deleted after 90 days, households kept out of MRV records | Pilot |
| Aadhaar | No Aadhaar image accepted as ID unless its QR signature is verified; the number is never stored ([UIDAI](https://old.uidai.gov.in/images/The_Aadhaar_Authentication_and_Offline_Verifications_Regulations_2021-_Clean_copy-30122025.pdf)) | Prefer a driving licence, voter ID, PAN, DigiLocker or a BBMP card | Pilot |
| Karnataka gig-worker law | Platform registers within 45 days; 1% welfare fee capped at ₹0.50–1.50 per job; 14 days' notice before removal ([PRS](https://prsindia.org/bills/states/the-karnataka-platform-based-gig-workers-social-security-and-welfare-bill-2025), [SCC](https://www.scconline.com/blog/post/2026/02/18/karnataka-government-notifies-gig-workers-welfare-fee-mandatory/)) | Saathi pay off-platform; payout ledger; appeal flow with a 14-day clock | Pilot |
| Hazardous streams | E-waste and batteries only to registered recyclers; child labour banned in battery, e-waste and plastics work | Authorised-buyer routing; business declarations; 18+ check for Saathis | Pilot |
| MSMED Act | Pay micro and small suppliers within 45 days ([Samadhaan](https://samadhaan.msme.gov.in/)) | Due-date clock on trades | Pilot |

Every tax or legal output is labelled 'for information, confirm with your CA'. A lawyer and a CA review the Rulebook before real users arrive.
sections.carbonSolar:
**Carbon: report impact and build credit-readiness. Mint nothing.** None of India's 8 approved offset methods credits recycling, CCC trading is only starting around Oct 2026 ([BEE](https://beeindia.gov.in/show_content.php?lang=1&level=1&ls_id=189&lid=294), [Carbon Pulse](https://carbon-pulse.com/365604/)), and recycling is not on India's Article 6.4 list ([MoEFCC](https://moef.gov.in/uploads/pdf/article_6.4.pdf)).

| Instrument | Unit and price | Our role | When |
|---|---|---|---|
| Plastic credits (Verra PWRM0001/0002, PCX) | 1 credit = 1 t; PCX lists $106–804/t ([PCX](https://www.pcxsolutions.org/post/pcx-solutions-releases-updated-plastic-credit-standard-mandates-third-party-verification)) | Bengaluru grouped project with a partner developer; lots marked credit-ready | Scale |
| Carbon credits (VMR0007, GS 448) | 2024 voluntary average $6.34/tCO2e ([SOVCM](https://3298623.fs1.hubspotusercontent-na1.net/hubfs/3298623/SOVCM%202025/Ecosystem%20Marketplace%20State%20of%20the%20Voluntary%20Carbon%20Market%202025.pdf)) | Metals only; paper has no active method | Scale |
| EPR certificates | Issued only by registered processors; traded on CPCB's exchange, which bars brokers ([EPRETP](https://cpcb.gov.in/openpdffile.php?id=TGF0ZXN0RmlsZS80MzBfMTczNTYzNzY5Nl9tZWRpYXBob3RvMTM5ODcucGRm)) | Evidence packs only | Pilot export, scale product |

- **Replace the v1 carbonCredits minting table** with three numbers per lot: kg diverted, indicative tCO2e (factor frozen per lot from a dated table) and credit-ready tonnes. Only registry serial numbers are ever called credits.
- **One claim per lot**, with a status of none, EPR certificate number, reserved, registry serial or retired. This blocks double counting across EPR certificates, plastic credits and carbon credits.
- **Credit-rights clause and a baseline declaration at onboarding in the pilot.** Verra requires ownership evidence from each instance's start date and validation within 2 years ([Verra PS](https://verra.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/02/Plastic-Waste-Reduction-Standard-v1.0.pdf)). A published revenue share, shown in the green-bonus preview, gives kabadiwalas and Saathis a reason to sign.
- **MRV weight is taken at dispatch** on a calibrated scale with a GRN and invoice ([PWRM0001](https://verra.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/06/PWRM0001_Plastic-Waste-Collection-Methodology-v1.1.pdf)). Doorstep half-kilo weighing stays for payment only.

**Solar: sell to our own yards and recyclers first, not to Bengaluru homes.** Karnataka has only 938 MW of rooftop solar out of India's 32.6 GW ([MNRE](https://cdnbbsr.s3waas.gov.in/s3716e1b8c6cd17b771da77391355749f3/uploads/2026/09/202609081073775955.pdf)), and Gruha Jyothi already makes the first 200 units free for homes.

| Case | System | Payback |
|---|---|---|
| Home paying its bill (LT-1, 350 units) | 3 kW, ₹57,000 after subsidy | 2.2–2.8 years |
| Gruha Jyothi home, net metering | 2 kW | 11–34 years (don't promote) |
| LT-5 yard, 2,500 units | 15 kW non-DCR | 3.2–5.4 years |
| HT-2(a) recycler, 60,000 units | 200 kW non-DCR | 2.5–3.5 years |

Sources: [KERC DSPV tariff](https://kerc.karnataka.gov.in/uploads/48561787653428.pdf), [KERC regulations](https://kerc.karnataka.gov.in/uploads/media_to_upload1787642381.pdf), [PM Surya Ghar](https://pib.gov.in/newsite/erelcontent.aspx?relid=292054).

- Build a calculator whose constants are dated config rows (tariffs, export rates, subsidy, CUF 100–138.7 kWh/kW/month), with a 'Your yard could save ₹X/month' card for businesses.
- Solar quotes go through a services request flow to verified installers, who become a new provider role. Charge installers, never consumers.
- Add a banner: net-metered projects commissioned after 31 Dec 2026 need domestic cells from ALMM List-II ([PIB](https://pib.gov.in/newsite/erelcontent.aspx?relid=291400)).
- Old panels and batteries are catalogue items routed only to registered recyclers.
sections.integrations:
**Integrate through exports and deep links first, and add APIs only where they exist and pay back.** Government portals have no public APIs (CPCB SWM and EPR, Swachhatam), and some sit behind CAPTCHAs (KSPCB XGN), so the admin checks those by hand.

| System | How | Cost | When |
|---|---|---|---|
| SMS (MSG91, already chosen) | Codes and receipts; add an '@luma.green #code' last line to every OTP template before DLT approval so Chrome can auto-fill it ([WebOTP](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/identity/web-apis/web-otp)) | Per SMS | Now |
| WhatsApp | wa.me links with the context pre-filled, and the Web Share API for PDFs; the Business app (free) for the help desk ([pricing](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/whatsapp/pricing/)) | ₹0 for chats the user starts | Now; Cloud API or MSG91 Hello at scale |
| Mapbox | Optimization v1 for today's route (up to 12 stops) ([docs](https://docs.mapbox.com/api/navigation/optimization-v1/)) | Free up to 100k requests a month | Now; VROOM for multi-vehicle routing at scale |
| UPI | Kabadiwala scans the household's UPI QR; UTR recorded | ₹0 P2P | Now |
| Tally | Excel files in Tally's import layout (Purchase, Receipt Note, Sales) ([Tally](https://help.tallysolutions.com/import-data-in-tally/)) | ₹0 | Now; XML after testing with accountants; connector at scale |
| CPCB EPR portal | Monthly purchase register CSV in portal field order ([manual](https://eprplastic.cpcb.gov.in/assets/pdfs/Guidance_Manual.pdf)) | ₹0 | Pilot |
| CPCB SWM portal / Swachhatam | Quarterly returns and ward totals as CSV | ₹0 | Pilot |
| KSPCB XGN, e-Mapan | Admin looks up consent and scale certificates by hand; number and expiry stored | ₹0 | Now |
| GSTN via a GSP | GSTIN status check at onboarding; e-invoice and e-way bill later ([GSTN](https://developer.gst.gov.in/apiportal/)) | Per call | Pilot / scale |
| DigiLocker via API Setu | Driving licence or PAN pulled with the user's consent ([API Setu](https://apisetu.gov.in/digilocker)) | Onboarding as a requester | Pilot |
| Razorpay Route / Cashfree | Virtual account (about ₹20 per payment) plus a held transfer (0.1–0.25%) ([Cashfree](https://www.cashfree.com/payment-gateway-charges/)) | About 0.3% per trade | Scale (needs ₹40 lakh turnover) |
| Speech (Sarvam or Chirp 3 HD) | Pre-recorded prompts; voice notes transcribed at about ₹0.25 each ([Sarvam](https://www.sarvam.ai/api-pricing)) | Low | Now (recorded); pilot (transcription) |
| Freight partners (Porter, Vahak), ONDC logistics | Freight estimate from our own rate table, booked with the yard's own transporter ([Porter](https://porter.in/trucks/bangalore)) | ₹0 | Scale |

There are no live exchange feeds (MCX, LME, BigMint) until a licence and legal review are done.
sections.support:
**The help model is a real person on WhatsApp or phone, backed by picture-and-voice step cards.** Text interfaces failed first-time low-literacy users, and a live operator was about 10 times more accurate ([Microsoft Research](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/publication/designing-mobile-interfaces-for-novice-and-low-literacy-users/)).

| Channel (pilot, 13–20 Oct) | Hours | First reply | Resolved within |
|---|---|---|---|
| One number for WhatsApp and calls | 8 AM–8 PM, every day | 15 min | Pickup-day issues the same day; others 24 h |
| In-app help form (convex/support.ts) | Any time | 2 h during hours | 24 h |
| Safety | Any time | Call back within 10 min | Same day |
| Saathi pay or removal complaint | — | 48 h | 14 days (Karnataka standard) |
| Application | — | — | 12–24 h |

- **Help button on every screen**: WhatsApp with role, screen and booking code pre-filled; Call; or the form. It costs nothing, because Meta doesn't charge for chats the user starts ([Meta](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/whatsapp/pricing/)).
- **Help hubs at /help/{role}**: 6–10 step cards and 8–12 FAQs each, stored as data keyed by role, topic, language and slug, with a 'Did this help?' tap logged to pilot events.
- **Languages for the pilot**: hand-checked text and human voice in Kannada, Tamil, Hindi, Urdu and English first, then Telugu and Bengali. The other locales show 'translation coming'.
- **Onboarding at the shop**: a 20–30 minute visit with a practice booking, a named 'digital buddy' and a laminated A5 picture card. Peer-made local video drove 7 times the adoption ([Digital Green](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/publication/digital-green-participatory-video-for-agricultural-extension/)).
- **Partners**: Hasiru Dala (2,314 trainings for 61,114 people, [Hasiru Dala](https://hasirudala.in/initiatives/training)) co-runs Saathi and DWCC onboarding.
- **Scale**: MSG91 Hello shared inbox (₹1,500–3,000/month, [MSG91](https://msg91.com/in/pricing/hello)), IVR with missed-call callback, and community trainers paid per active user.
sections.standards:
**Luma.Green sets the norms by publishing them openly, starting with material codes and a receipt format.** Standards-based network effects rank second of 16 types ([NFX](https://www.nfx.com/post/network-effects-bible)), and ReMA's free scrap specifications are the trade's common language ([ReMA](https://www.isrispecs.org/)).

| Standard | What it fixes | Version / owner |
|---|---|---|
| Luma Material Codes (LMC) | ASCII codes in the existing FAMILY-GRADE form (PAPER-NEWS), never renamed or reused. Each code has names in 12 languages, local aliases, HSN code, unit and GST unit code, ReMA/ISRI or IS 2549 grade, EPR category, value class, and hazardous and authorised-buyer flags ([tariff 7404](https://www.eximguru.com/indian-customs-duty/7404-copper-waste-and-scrap.aspx), [3915](https://www.eximguru.com/hs-codes/3915-waste-parings-and-scrap-of.aspx)) | v0.1.0 under CC BY 4.0; public page with JSON and CSV |
| Hand-off receipt | Lot ID, parent lots, sender and receiver IDs, material code, gross, tare, deduction and reason, net grams, rate in paise, payment method and UTR, scale ID, slip photo hash, time and geohash | v0.1 JSON schema, published with the codes |
| Weighing norm | Stamped scale (Legal Metrology), a photo of the reading, both sides confirm; no adjustment within ±1% on B2B loads, as ISRI does for domestic loads ([ISRI](https://www.isrispecs.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/04/isri-specs2024final.pdf)) | Platform rule |
| Grade cards | Default limits per material: paper moisture ≤12%; OCC prohibitives ≤1% and prohibitives plus outthrows ≤5%; tuned with Bengaluru yards | Admin-edited table |
| Luma Verified badge | Checks passed and date; consent validity; scale stamp expiry; withdrawn if rules are broken | Platform rule |
| Local names | Collected from 10 pilot kabadiwalas with voice clips and stored as aliases, never display names (seesa means lead, sheesha means glass) | Pilot sprint |

- Rates, GST and emission factors live in separate dated tables keyed by code, so a rate change never rewrites a receipt.
- Governance: anyone can propose a change, versions are numbered, and an advisory group of kabadiwalas, yards, a recycler and Hasiru Dala reviews changes. Offer the codes to a neutral body (IARPMA/MRAI or a BIS committee) once others use them.
- We cite ISRI code words and numbers but write our own definitions, because the ISRI text is copyrighted.

modules.name: Sell (household)
modules.purpose: Turn a photo into a booked pickup or drop-off with a fair, visible price and no account.
features: Photo to AI estimate limited to about 20 household codes, priced from Luma tables; 'no cash value, free take-away' for zero-value items
Nearby verified shops side by side with their rates for these materials, distance, hours and badges; best price tagged
Pickup time slots with a limit per kabadiwala, a minimum load (default 15 kg) and a drop-off code for small loads
Vehicle fit from estimated kg and bulk
Booking confirmed by SMS code; tracking link showing when, who and how much; ETA while on the way
Auto re-offer to the next shop after a 15-minute timeout; self-serve cancel and reschedule
Receipt confirmed with a handover code; recycle points as an impact count with no cash value

modules.name: Shop (kabadiwala)
modules.purpose: Give a low-literacy shop owner a phone-first workday: requests, route, weigh, pay, sort, sell.
features: Requests with Accept/Reject, read-aloud and auto-accept
Today's route (Mapbox, up to 12 stops) and 'I'm on the way'
Weigh-and-pay: half-kilo steppers, scale photo per material, cash or UPI with optional UTR
Rate card above the floor, with a buys / takes free / doesn't take flag per material
Stock and sorting runs (mixed paper in, newspaper, cardboard and reject out)
Publish stock to yards; accept pooled-collection invites
Scale register with Legal Metrology stamp expiry and reminder

modules.name: Exchange (B2B)
modules.purpose: Match kabadiwala stock to yards, and yard bales to recyclers and manufacturers, with documents at every step.
features: Two-way stock board: sellers post what they have, buyers post what they want; accept or make one counter-offer
Pooled collection: fill one vehicle from several shops, with a capacity bar for kg and volume
Gate screen: weigh-in and weigh-out, slip photo, both sides' weights, flag above 1%
Quality check with grade card, deductions with photo and reason, accept / deduct / reject
Trade timeline: requested, accepted, funded (simulated escrow), dispatched, weighed, released
Trade document pack PDF: PO, weight slips, quality result, GRN, invoice, e-way bill number
Freight estimate from an admin vehicle-rate table

modules.name: Prices
modules.purpose: Keep prices fair, dated and editable without code, and publish a trusted Bengaluru board.
features: Admin price console: floors, fallbacks, bands, suspend switch per material, CSV paste, audit log
Reference prices (admin and investor views only) with source and date
Public board /prices/bengaluru with Live/Guide status and a sample-data badge
'Where your rupee goes' chart for newspaper and aluminium cans
Daily 06:00 IST calculation with a circuit breaker (pilot)
Freshness reminders and an honour rate per shop (pilot)

modules.name: Trace and documents
modules.purpose: Make every kilogram traceable from household to factory, and export it in the formats buyers and regulators already use.
features: Lot passport: QR per lot or bale, parent lots, map timeline, weights, photos, receipts
Mass-balance check: warns when sales exceed receipts or declared capacity
Read-only share link for auditors and brands
Exports: Tally Excel, CPCB EPR purchase register CSV, SWM quarterly return CSV
One-claim-per-lot status (none, EPR certificate, reserved, registry serial, retired)

modules.name: Payments
modules.purpose: Record every rupee now, and move to licensed escrow only when volume and eligibility allow.
features: Payment method on every receipt: cash, P2P UPI or merchant UPI, plus UTR
Verified payout account with the holder's name matched
Simulated escrow with a live breakdown of GST, 0.5% TCS, 0.1% TDS and fees (prototype)
Due dates with the MSME 45-day clock; cash-limit warnings above ₹10,000 per person per day
Razorpay Route escrow with a virtual account, or bank escrow with a trustee for large orders (scale)

modules.name: Trust and verification
modules.purpose: Verify every business and person by hand, show the result, and resolve disputes quickly.
features: Verification queue with a checklist per role and a 12–24 h clock
Badges: phone, documents, scale verified, site verified, consent valid until <date>
Registrations stored as rows: GSTIN, KSPCB consent, CPCB EPR, SWM or local-body registration, Udyam
ID checks without Aadhaar numbers: driving licence, voter ID, PAN, DigiLocker, BBMP card
'Something's wrong' complaints with 48 h and 30-day timers; account pause with reason and appeal
Two-way ratings only from code-confirmed pickups
Weight-trust view: weighed vs estimated kg against the city median

modules.name: Saathi work
modules.purpose: Give gig workers safe, visible, fairly treated work while pay stays off-platform in the pilot.
features: Onboarding with area, radius, work types, vehicle, ID and selfie
Saathi Ready: 5 picture cards, picture quiz and a badge
Job cards: pay shown before accepting, hazards and PPE, right to refuse
SOS button, incident report, 14-day appeal
Work register (days, kg, pay) exportable for NAMASTE, e-Shram and the Karnataka welfare board

modules.name: Compliance
modules.purpose: Turn changing Indian rules into data and reminders instead of code.
features: Rulebook: every threshold, rate and deadline with an effective-from date
Tax flags per trade: e-way bill, metal reverse charge with self-invoice, 2% GST TDS, TCS on scrap
Compliance vault: consent number, colour category and validity; EPR and PWP registration; installed capacity
Calendar: GSTR-7 and GSTR-8, SWM returns, consent expiry, scale re-verification, yearly dark-pattern audit
Authorised-buyer routing for batteries, e-waste, tyres and used oil

modules.name: Impact: EPR, carbon and solar
modules.purpose: Sell verified evidence, not certificates, and add clean-energy services for the chain.
features: Impact counter: kg diverted, indicative tCO2e, credit-ready tonnes

result.helpCentre:
## Help centre plan

The help centre lives at /help/{role} and a public /help index. Each guide is 3–6 step cards (icon, screenshot, one line, voice), and each FAQ is a question with a one-line answer. Every item ends with **Still stuck? WhatsApp · Call · Write to us**. Content is stored as data keyed by role, topic, language and slug. [decide] marks answers that need a founder decision.

### Every hub
- **Change language?** Tap the language button at the top and pick one of 12.
- **SMS code didn't come?** Wait 30 seconds, tap Resend, and check the number; if it still fails, WhatsApp us.
- **Install the app?** In Chrome, tap Install or 'Add to Home screen'.
- **Can't read well?** Tap the speaker on any card, or send us a voice note.
- **Reach a person?** WhatsApp or call the support number, 8 AM–8 PM every day.
- **My data?** We keep only what we need to verify you and run bookings; ask us to see or delete it.

### Household (no account)
Guides: Sell in 3 steps · Take photos that estimate well · Book a pickup · Drop off at a shop · Track your pickup · Weighing and payment at the door · Cancel or change · Your points.
- **Need an account?** No; you confirm your mobile once with an SMS code.
- **What do you take?** Paper, cardboard, plastic, metal and glass; batteries and e-waste go only to authorised recyclers; no food, sanitary or medical waste.
- **Why a different amount from the estimate?** You're paid for the weighed kilos at the shop's rate; the photo gives only a range.
- **Who sets the price?** Each shop sets its own, never below Luma.Green's minimum.
- **How am I paid?** Cash or UPI from the kabadiwala before they leave; Luma.Green only records it.
- **The weight looks wrong?** Ask for a re-weigh in front of you, don't give the handover code, and tap 'Something's wrong'.
- **Pickup charge?** [decide] Proposed: free in the pilot; small loads are better as drop-off.
- **No shop accepted?** After 15 minutes we offer the booking to the next shop and SMS you.
- **Who sees my address?** Only the kabadiwala who accepts, after they accept.
- **Photos?** Used for the estimate and deleted after 90 days.

### Kabadiwala
Guides: Join · After you apply · Set my prices · Accept or reject · Auto-accept · Today's route · Weigh and pay · Record sorting · Show stock to yards · Add my scale.
- **Need GST?** No; mark 'Not GST-registered'.
- **Verification time?** 12–24 hours; we call your login number.
- **Commission?** None in the pilot. [decide] what comes after.
- **Why a minimum price?** So households get a fair rate; you can always pay more.
- **Why a scale photo?** It protects you in a dispute and earns the 'Scale verified' badge.
- **What is the handover code?** The household's 4 digits; the pickup completes only when you enter it.
- **No vehicle?** Switch off home pickups; households can still drop off at your shop.
- **Customer not home?** Call from Today, then WhatsApp us the booking code. [decide] the no-show rule.
- **Account paused?** The screen shows why; tap Appeal.

### Yard / DWCC
Guides: Join as a yard · Upload consent and machine photos · 'Consent not required' (paper baling) · Find stock · Pooled collection · Gate weighing · Quality and deductions · Export to Tally.
- **Which consent?** KSPCB consent in Karnataka, or your state board's; we check it on the public register.
- **Is GST required?** Optional now; you'll need it to buy metal from unregistered kabadiwalas (reverse charge).
- **When is an e-way bill needed?** For a motor-vehicle load over ₹50,000; the app tells you per load.
- **Weights differ?** No adjustment within 1%; above that, the certified slip decides.
- **Who pays freight?** Set 'yard collects' or 'kabadiwala delivers' per trade.
- **More than one yard?** One address per account; WhatsApp us to add more.

### Recycler
Guides: Join · Upload consent and PWP registration · Find sorted lots · Order from a yard · Publish output · Export the EPR register · Open a lot passport.
- **Plastic extra?** Add your CPCB Plastic Waste Processor registration.
- **Does Luma issue EPR certificates?** No; we give you evidence to back yours.
- **Payments?** Recorded now; escrow is planned.
- **Capacity warning?** We warn at 80% and 100% of your declared yearly capacity.

### Manufacturer
Guides: Join (one PDF) · See recycler output · Place an order · Trace a lot · Team roles.
- **What do I need?** Business details and your pollution-board certificate; GST optional.
- **Recycled-content proof?** Open the lot passport or share its read-only link.
- **Pay through Luma?** Not yet; escrow is planned.

### Saathi
Guides: Join · Photo ID and selfie · Saathi Ready · Take a job · Do a home pickup · Get help fast.
- **Which ID?** Driving licence, voter ID, PAN, DigiLocker document or BBMP waste-picker card.
- **Who pays me?** The shop or company you work for, directly; pay is shown before you accept.
- **Can I say no?** Yes, always.
- **Hurt or unsafe?** Call 112, then us; we call back within 10 minutes.
- **Paused?** We show the reason; appeals are answered within 14 days.
- **Police verification?** [decide] Likely required for home pickups (Seva Sindhu certificate).

### Observers (investor, brand, city)
- **Is this real data?** No; the prototype shows sample data, badged on every number.
- **Can I export?** Yes, CSV from each dashboard.

### Admin (internal)
Guides: Verify an application · Ask for changes · Answer a request · Weight dispute · Safety incident · Pause and appeal · Edit a price or rule · Edit a help card.
- **Full Aadhaar uploaded?** Delete it and ask for another ID.
- **Underpaid household?** Compare weighed kg × rate card and the scale photo; warn the shop.

risks: Investors may read seeded numbers as traction. Mitigation: a sample-data badge on every number, seed data kept separate, and the prototype called a prototype in every deck.

Direct overlap with Scrapr's partner-kabadiwala marketplace in 25+ Bengaluru areas. Mitigation: lead the pitch with the traced chain, the photo estimate, Kannada-first voice and the yard tools, not with 'a kabadiwala marketplace'.

Household pickups lose money (45–60 minutes per order; a hired Tata Ace costs ₹9.2/kg on a 25 kg lot). Mitigation: minimum loads, drop-off as the default, slot limits, the kabadiwala's own vehicle, and apartment pickup days.

Kabadiwalas may turn against factory reference prices shown to households, or trade off-platform to avoid fees. Mitigation: reference prices go to admin and investor views only, no doorstep commission, and the value to kabadiwalas comes from tools and yard access.

Handling trade money without an authorised aggregator is illegal, and escrow switches on GST TCS, income-tax TDS and seller registration. Mitigation: record-only in the pilot, simulated escrow in the demo, and Route or bank escrow only after legal and CA sign-off.

EPR and carbon mis-positioning: calling our records certificates, or minting credits in the v1 carbonCredits table, would not survive due diligence and could draw greenwashing complaints. Mitigation: sell evidence only; only registry serial numbers are called credits.

Fraud through the platform: fake pickups, light scales, circular trades like the ₹2,384 crore Karnataka case, and stolen copper cable. Mitigation: handover codes, scale photos, two-sided weights, mass-balance checks, related-account merging and theft-risk flags.

Gig-worker law: Luma.Green may count as an aggregator for Saathi jobs (registration within 45 days, 1% fee, 14 days' notice before removal). Mitigation: pay stays off-platform, a payout ledger from day one, and an appeal flow.

Privacy: ID photos, selfies, household addresses and migrant workers' data, with DPDP penalties up to ₹250 crore and UIDAI rules on Aadhaar. Mitigation: no Aadhaar numbers, 90-day photo deletion, households kept out of MRV records, and totals only for cities.

Hazardous streams (batteries, e-waste, tyres, used oil) sent to unauthorised buyers would create legal and reputational liability. Mitigation: authorised-buyer routing; keep them out of the open pilot market until checks exist.

A single admin cannot verify, price, support and judge disputes at scale, and pricing plus dispute judging in one person is a conflict of interest. Mitigation: rulebook data, clocks, and a second operator before the pilot expands.
Rules change constantly (six or more legal numbers since Jul 2024; KERC tariffs twice in 2026). Mitigation: every threshold is a dated admin row and every tax output is labelled for information.

Waste-picker politics in Bengaluru: a platform seen as displacing pickers will meet resistance. Mitigation: co-design with Hasiru Dala and the union, DWCCs as yards, and the Saathi work record helping them get recognised.
The UPI merchant fee (0.4% above ₹2,000 from 15 Oct 2026) and metal reverse charge may push B2B trades back to cash. Mitigation: record the method and steer larger payments to NEFT with a UTR.
openQuestions: Does Luma.Green count as an 'e-commerce operator' for the 0.1% income-tax TDS and for GST while money stays off-platform? This needs a CA opinion before B2B trades.
Is Saathi work 'platform-based gig work' under the Karnataka law when the kabadiwala pays the Saathi directly, and what welfare-fee category applies?

Which Greater Bengaluru Authority corporation and which Hasiru Dala-supported DWCC will co-run the pilot, and will GBA recognise verified kabadiwalas as authorised collectors under the SWM Rules 2026?
What gross margin does a Bengaluru kabadiwala keep per material, what minimum load makes a home pickup worthwhile, and do households choose the nearest shop or the best price?
Who pays freight between kabadiwala and yard, what are the usual credit terms (cash vs 7–30 days), and what lot sizes are typical per material?
Which words do Bengaluru kabadiwalas actually use for each material (Delhi slang vs English vs Kannada), and are milk pouches a separate paid stream?
Founder decisions for the help centre: pickup charge or minimum, what recycle points are worth, business fees after the pilot, the no-show rule, Saathi insurance and police verification.
Will registered recyclers, PROs and auditors accept Luma.Green's weight, photo and trace records as supporting evidence, and would brands pay per tonne for them?
Should the pilot exclude batteries and e-waste entirely until authorised-buyer routing and CPCB/KSPCB checks are live?
Can a Gruha Jyothi household take gross metering and keep its 200 free units? Ask BESCOM before showing any home solar case.
Which escrow route fits first: Razorpay Route once Luma has ₹40 lakh of turnover, onboarding each yard as its own merchant, or a bank escrow with a trustee?
Who long-term owns the Luma Material Codes: Luma.Green, an industry association, or a BIS committee, and under which licence after v1?

result.verdict: The plan mostly holds up against the briefs. Most numbers trace to a cited source, it is right to keep money off the platform and to sell evidence rather than certificates, and treating the rules as data is the correct call. It is not ready to present or to build from yet, for four reasons. (1) The headline claim, tracing one recycler bale back to individual household pickups, cannot work physically: a 2,000 kg PET lot cannot come from 14 household receipts, and yards pool and re-sort material. The plan never says whether tracing uses mass balance or segregated lots. (2) Several investor-facing numbers compare unlike things or use old data presented as current: household cans against primary MCX aluminium, and the 2014 mill price for newspaper. (3) The plan drops legal risks the briefs raised: competition law on the admin price floors, the national Social Security Code rules for gig aggregators, enforcement under SWM r.17 against unregistered kabadiwalas who become visible, liability for abetting false EPR claims, DPDP's one-year retention rule against 90-day photo deletion, and the fact that the CPCB EPR exchange is not yet live. It also contradicts itself: it says exchange prices are never shown publicly, then puts MCX on the public price chart. It says a lawyer and CA review everything before real users arrive, but pilot users arrive 3 days after the prototype. It gates escrow on ₹40 lakh of Luma's own turnover while charging nothing until 2027. (4) The prototype scope is 13 features plus a UX overhaul and 13 demo scripts in about 9 working days (29 Sep–10 Oct). Cut it to about 6 core flows and make the rest static or seeded.

gaps.issue: The lot passport says it traces 'one bale back to the individual household pickups it came from', and the demo walks PET bale LOT-0412 back to 14 household receipts. A household sells about 1–3 kg of PET, and the demo trade is 2,000 kg. Yards also pool and sort material from many sources, most of it bought off the platform from waste pickers and walk-ins. So the claim is physically impossible, and a diligent investor or auditor will spot it. None of the briefs supports household-level physical identity. The ISCC PLUS finding separates mass balance from physical segregation.
gaps.fix: Choose and state a tracing method: mass-balance allocation, or segregated lots only. Change the passport to show 'X kg (Y%) of this bale is linked to Luma receipts; the rest is declared supply from named off-platform sources'. Reseed LOT-0412 so the numbers add up, for example about 180 kg of PET from 2 kabadiwalas, of which 22 kg is from household receipts. Rewrite the lead line as 'every hand-off recorded', not 'traced to individual households'.

gaps.issue: The public price board's 'Where your rupee goes' chart and the market table put household cans (₹60) next to MCX primary aluminium (₹347.50) and call it about 17%. Cans are scrap, not ingot. The pricing brief itself gives UBC lots at ₹120–290 and Bengaluru utensil scrap at ₹215–220, which would make the share about 20–50%. The chart also uses newspaper 'mill ₹14–15', a 2014 BBMP figure, while the pricing brief puts current mill-grade ONP at about ₹20.
gaps.fix: Compare cans with UBC scrap asking prices, labelled as asking prices with source and date. Label the ₹10→11→12–13→14–15 newspaper chain as 'Bengaluru 2014 (BBMP study)', and add a separate 2026 point (door ₹10, mill-grade ONP about ₹20, Mumbai listing). Apply the same fix to the market table row.

gaps.issue: The plan contradicts itself on exchange data. The pricing section says reference prices are for admin and investors only and nothing from an exchange is shown publicly. Yet the prototype scope puts the MCX-derived 17% cans share on the public /prices/bengaluru page. The pricing brief's pilot rule is 'no exchange number on screen', and MCX forbids public display without an agreement. The market brief warns that showing factory prices to households may turn kabadiwalas against the platform.
gaps.fix: Take every MCX, LME or BigMint figure, and every ratio calculated from one, off public and household screens. Keep them in the admin view. In the investor view, show them only as 'sourced citations', typed in by hand, with no live feed. Build the public 'rupee' chart only from dated surveys and Luma's own chain data.

gaps.issue: Competition-law risk has been dropped. The pricing brief flags that a platform-set floor and fallback, if competing kabadiwalas all copy it, can look like fixing buying prices under Competition Act s.3. The plan's floors (75% of the 28-day median), suggested fallbacks and 'best price' ranking are exactly what that warning covers. No risk or open question mentions it.
gaps.fix: Add this as a risk and an open question for counsel. Present the floor as a household-protection minimum. Never show the fallback to kabadiwalas as a suggested price. Let shops set any price above the floor, and record that they priced it themselves.

gaps.issue: The national Social Security Code is missing from the compliance section. The legal and personas briefs cover the Social Security (Central) Rules, in force 8 May 2026: aggregators register on Shram Suvidha, upload workers within 45 days, report joins and exits in real time, and pay 1–2% of turnover capped at 5% of payouts. The plan covers only Karnataka. Its mitigation, 'pay stays off-platform', does not remove the risk, because the Karnataka Act covers work booked through an app, and the demo has Saathis accepting job cards in the app.
gaps.fix: Add a Code on Social Security row to the compliance table. In the pilot, do not dispatch Saathi jobs through the app until counsel gives an opinion on 'aggregator' status under both laws. Until then, Saathis are onboarded and trained only, with 'jobs coming soon'. Keep the payout ledger in the design.

gaps.issue: SWM Rules 2026, r.17 imposes environmental compensation on anyone collecting or sorting without registration. The public-systems brief warns that making informal kabadiwalas visible to officials could expose them before they register. The plan's ward dashboards, Swachhatam exports and waste-picker registry exports carry no such warning.
gaps.fix: Add this as a risk. City exports carry totals only. Share any business-level data with a city only with that business's consent and once it holds a registration number. Add a 'help me register' task for kabadiwalas and yards in onboarding.

gaps.issue: The plan leaves out liability for abetting EPR violations. The EPR brief notes that the used-oil and battery rules reach anyone who aids or abets a violation, and that a partner's over-claim becomes that partner's legal problem. The plan's EPR risk covers only 'calling records certificates'.
gaps.fix: Add this as a risk. Records must be tamper-evident, as the append-only design already intends. Evidence packs should state capacity against claimed volume. Contracts with recyclers and PROs should say that Luma's records are supporting evidence, not certification.

gaps.issue: The plan treats the EPR exchange as live. The carbon section says certificates are 'traded on CPCB's exchange, which bars brokers'. The EPR and B2B briefs say MSTC built the exchange but it was still unapproved in June 2026, and certificates currently move directly on the CPCB portals.
gaps.fix: Reword: 'a CPCB-authorised exchange (built by MSTC, approval pending as of Jun 2026) will host trading and bars brokers; today certificates transfer on the portals.' Keep 'read exchange prices via API' at scale, conditional on launch.

gaps.issue: The number of approved offset methods conflicts across briefs. The plan says 'none of India's 8 approved offset methods credits recycling', citing IETA from March 2025. The business brief cites the ICM portal listing 12 approved methods.
gaps.fix: Say 'none of the approved ICM methodologies (8 per IETA, Mar 2025; the ICM portal now lists 12) covers material recycling', and check the portal before the deck is final.

gaps.issue: The plan misses an additionality problem for plastic credits. The carbon brief notes that under PWRM0001 Step 1, collecting plastic already covered by mandatory EPR is not additional unless compliance is below 50%. Yet the plan pitches a Bengaluru grouped plastic-credit project and shows 'credit-ready tonnes' next to $106–804/t pricing.
gaps.fix: Add this as a risk. Mark credit-readiness per material with an additionality flag. Keep plastic-credit revenue out of the base case in investor material, and take it out of the impact counter's implied value.

gaps.issue: The credit-rights clause in the pilot is under-specified and risky. Low-literacy kabadiwalas and Saathis would be asked to assign environmental attributes with no defined revenue share, no lawyer-reviewed text, and no chosen project start date. The Verra 2-year validation clock runs from the start of collection.
gaps.fix: Keep the clause out of the pilot until a lawyer approves a plain-language version in the user's language. It should be revocable until project registration, and include a published minimum share. Record the baseline declaration now, since that is harmless. Pick the project start date deliberately.

gaps.issue: Photo deletion conflicts with DPDP retention. The plan deletes household photos after 90 days. The legal brief notes that DPDP Rules r.8(3) requires personal data, traffic data and logs to be kept for at least one year, and that IT Rules require registration data to be kept for 180 days after closure.
gaps.fix: Have counsel reconcile the two. A likely approach: delete the image at 90 days but keep a hash and metadata log for a year, and state this in the notice. Add a row to the compliance table.

gaps.issue: Escrow eligibility does not add up. The Phase 2 gate needs a 'first escrow trade through Route once the ₹40 lakh eligibility is met'. That limit is Luma's own GST-3B turnover, not trade volume. Every revenue stream is ₹0 until 2027, and society and yard plans at ₹500–5,000 a month will not reach ₹40 lakh by June 2027. Luma also needs GST registration for that turnover to show at all.
gaps.fix: Set the Phase 2 escrow route to a bank escrow with a trustee (RazorpayX Escrow+ or CastlerX), or onboard each yard as its own merchant. Keep Route as a later option. Add 'Luma GST registration' and 'TAN' to Phase 1 actions.

gaps.issue: The legal review cannot happen before real users arrive. The compliance section says a lawyer and CA review the Rulebook before real users arrive, but Phase 0 ends 10 Oct and the pilot starts 13 Oct. The roadmap lists the CA and lawyer review as a pilot goal.
gaps.fix: Either start the pilot with household pickups only (recorded, no B2B trades, no Saathi jobs, no credit clause) and add B2B trades after the review, or book the review for 6–12 Oct and make it a gate for pilot start.

gaps.issue: The prototype is far too big for the time available. There are 13 features, including a map with a capacity bar for pooled collection, PDF document packs, a 12-language standards page, a brand evidence view, a solar card, a Saathi quiz, help hubs with voice, and an AI estimate. On top of that come the Phase 0 UX fixes (button sizes, lakh formatting, contrast, voice in 3 languages), 13 demo scripts at 360×800 and a written A-to-Z test guide, all in about 9 working days. Voice clips in Kannada and Hindi also need review by native speakers.
gaps.fix: Must-demo: sell flow with proof of pickup, lot passport (fixed as above), simulated trade timeline, investor dashboard, and admin verification with the price console. Seeded or static: the stock board as a list with a capacity number instead of a map, a static sample PDF, the standards page in English and Kannada plus JSON, the brand view as a read-only passport link, the solar card as one static card, and one help hub with a single Kannada clip. Defer the Saathi quiz to the pilot. Cut the demo scripts to about 6.

gaps.issue: The pilot's language order ignores the plan's own census figures. Telugu (14%) comes after Hindi (4.6%) and Urdu (13%), and is left out of the Phase 1 list ('Kannada, Tamil, Urdu, Hindi and English') even though personas list Telugu speakers. Urdu RTL testing is not scheduled either.
gaps.fix: Order the pilot languages Kannada, Tamil, Telugu, Urdu, then Hindi/English, matched to the pilot wards. Add a native-speaker check of Urdu RTL layout before 13 Oct.

gaps.issue: The PWA cannot currently be installed. The help centre tells users to 'tap Install', but the design brief found the manifest lists only /logo.svg. Chrome needs 192 px and 512 px PNG icons before it offers installation. This is missing from Phase 0.
gaps.fix: Add PNG and maskable icons, screenshots and shortcuts to manifest.ts in Phase 0, and test the install prompt on Chrome for Android.

gaps.issue: Demo seed data rules are missing. The legal brief says investor demos must use fictitious GSTINs, consent numbers and business names, never ones copied from the public XGN register. The plan names 'GreenLoop Polymers' and a 'Peenya yard' with no check that these are not real businesses.
gaps.fix: Add a seed rule: GSTINs, consent numbers and names that are obviously fictitious, checked against XGN, MCA and Google. Put a 'Sample data' badge on names as well as on numbers.

gaps.issue: The weighing records risk being passed off as certified. The market brief warns that weights recorded in the app are not certified under Legal Metrology law, and that receipts must never be marketed as certified weights. The lead says 'confirmed weight', and the gate screen and evidence packs are pitched as proof.
gaps.fix: Add this as a risk. Label receipts 'recorded weight on scale #ID (stamp valid until <date>)'. The stamped scale or weighbridge slip remains the legal instrument.

gaps.issue: The market size includes material Luma cannot reach. The ₹1.8–2.1 lakh crore figure ('Luma.Green sits on') counts about 25% imported ferrous scrap and about 7 Mt of imported recovered paper (the materials brief puts domestic collection at about 13 Mt, against the plan's 17 Mt).
gaps.fix: Show the domestic share separately: roughly ₹1.2–1.3 lakh crore for ferrous at 75%, and paper at about 13 Mt. Or say 'reaching Indian mills, including imports'. Keep the 'our bottom-up floor' label.

gaps.issue: A local competitor is treated only as a partner. Hasiru Dala Innovations sells fair-trade, blockchain-traceable plastic to brands (Unilever, H&M) and has 327 supplier clients. The plan casts HDI only as a partner that supplies DWCCs and Saathis, while Luma plans to sell the same brand evidence.
gaps.fix: Add a competitor or conflict row for HDI's traceable-plastic line. In partnership talks, settle who owns the brand relationship and how the data is shared before building brand evidence packs.

gaps.issue: The pilot has no decision on e-waste and batteries. The catalogue marks EWASTE-* and BATTERY codes as household-level cash items the AI can estimate, while an open question asks whether to exclude them. The legal briefs say e-waste may be collected only by registered entities and that battery handling needs authorised transport.
gaps.fix: Decide now: hide A and Hz codes from the pilot's AI estimate and kabadiwala rate cards. Show 'we'll connect you to an authorised collector or brand take-back' instead.

gaps.issue: Some legal duties are left out of the compliance table: CERT-In 6-hour incident reporting and 180-day log retention; the IT Rules point that Arabic is not an Eighth-Schedule language, so binding terms for Arabic users must be English or Urdu; an 18+ confirmation for households; and income-tax TCS on scrap (s.394, 1% proposed to rise to 2%) with the manufacturing-declaration exemption. The TCS line is also missing from the ₹89,680 trade demo breakdown.
gaps.fix: Add these rows. Add a scrap-TCS line to the simulated breakdown showing 'declaration given → ₹0'.

gaps.issue: Two service levels cannot be met by one founder. The support levels (8 AM–8 PM every day, 15-minute first reply, 10-minute safety callback) and the 12–24 h verification promise all fall on one person, while auto-accept lets bookings arrive at night. The risk is noted only 'before the pilot expands'.
gaps.fix: Name a rota of at least 2 people before 13 Oct. Limit auto-accept to shop hours during the pilot. Publish service levels the team can actually meet.

gaps.issue: EPR for non-ferrous metal scrap, in force from 1 Apr 2026 according to the B2B brief (the EPR brief says it needs verification), is missing. Metals dominate the value of kabadiwala trade, but the plan's EPR and brand evidence covers plastics only.
gaps.fix: Add an open question to verify the rule. If it is confirmed, add copper, aluminium and brass lots to the evidence-pack roadmap.

gaps.issue: Integration costs mix two providers. Razorpay Route is listed at 'about ₹20 per payment' for the virtual account, but ₹20 is Cashfree's price. The WebOTP '@luma.green #code' line may also push Kannada and Hindi OTPs into a second SMS segment, a cost the design brief flagged.
gaps.fix: Quote per-provider prices, or say 'one aggregator, about 0.3%'. Check the length of the Unicode OTP template before submitting it for DLT approval.

unsupportedClaims: Lead: one bale can be traced back to 'the individual household pickups it came from'. No brief supports physical identity at household level after pooling and baling, and the demo figures (14 receipts in a 2,000 kg PET trade) do not add up.
Lead: Luma's receipts are 'the missing evidence behind' the ₹2,384 crore case. That case involved circular invoicing of tungsten-carbide scrap by shell firms, not the household-to-kabadiwala chain.
'Household gets about 17% of the aluminium price for cans'. This compares can scrap with primary MCX aluminium; against UBC scrap (₹120–290) the share is about 20–50%.
Newspaper 'mill ₹14–15' in the 'Where your rupee goes' demo. This is 2014 BBMP data; the pricing brief puts current mill-grade ONP at about ₹20/kg.
'None of India's 8 approved offset methods'. The business brief cites 12 approved methodologies on the ICM portal.
'EPR certificates ... traded on CPCB's exchange, which bars brokers', stated as current. The exchange was still awaiting approval in June 2026.
'Luma.Green sits on at least ₹1.8–2.1 lakh crore a year'. The figure includes imported ferrous scrap (about 25%) and about 7 Mt of imported recovered paper.
'Paper adds about 17 Mt of recovered fibre'. The materials brief (IPPTA) puts domestic collection at about 13 Mt plus 7 Mt imported.
'No competitor connects household bookings, kabadiwala tools and yard-to-factory trade'. This holds only for the 18 platforms reviewed; Kabadiwalla Connect (Chennai) comes close.
'A Kannada-first app' as a differentiator. The briefs checked only competitors' iOS listings; Android language support was not verified.
'Mills will pay for supply that is sorted and traceable'. This is the brief's inference ('should pay'), not evidence.
'80–85% of Bengaluru's dry waste passes through informal hands', presented as current. The source is a 2014 study.
'119 of 198 DWCCs are still operating', stated without noting the conflicting 164 figure (Nov 2025).
'Razorpay Route ... about ₹20 per payment'. The ₹20 figure is Cashfree's virtual-account price.
UPI 0.4% merchant fee from 15 Oct 2026. It rests on one secondary news source with no NPCI circular cited.
E-way bill threshold 'over ₹50,000 in Karnataka' for intra-state movement. The source is ClearTax, and the legal brief lists it as an open question.
Karnataka gig law 'Platform registers within 45 days', cited to the PRS Bill page rather than the enacted Act or notified rules.
The 'Consent valid till 2031' and 'scale stamp checked' demo details imply admin checks on e-Mapan and XGN that are not yet built or seeded.
